jobs.title: Analyst, Data Science - Burson
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Burson, part of WPP, is the global communications leader built to create value for clients through reputation. With highly specialized teams, industry-leading technologies and breakthrough creative, we help brands and businesses redefine reputation as a competitive advantage so they can lead today and into the future. When you work at Burson, you are part of a global community of lifelong learners who thrive at the edge of innovation.

WPP (LSE/NYSE: WPP) is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. For more information, visit WPP.com

For more information visit bursonglobal.com and follow us on LinkedIn and Instagram.

More About The Role

We are seeking a hands-on Analyst, Data Science
to join Burson’s Insights & Intelligence (I&I)
team.

The I&I team sits at the heart of Burson’s work, turning data into strategic insights that drive storytelling, campaign performance, and business outcomes. With an expanding client roster and growing scopes of work, our best-in-class team supports some of the world’s most recognizable global brands, including The Coca-Cola Company, Verizon, and Google.

This is a great opportunity for someone early in their data science career who is excited to apply technical and analytical skills to real-world business, marketing, and communications challenges. Working alongside data scientists, analysts, engineers, and strategists, you’ll support data science, dashboarding, and AI-driven initiatives that turn complex data into clear, actionable insights.

The ideal candidate has 1–2 years of relevant experience
and a strong foundation in Python, SQL, statistics, and data analysis. We’re looking for someone who is intellectually curious, comfortable working with complex datasets, and eager to continue developing their technical and client-facing skills.

What You'll Do

Support the end-to-end delivery of data science and analytics projects, including data preparation, analysis, modeling, visualization, and documentation
Assist with the development, testing, and refinement of predictive models, including time-series, forecasting, and machine learning solutions
Write and maintain code in Python, SQL, and/or R to clean, transform, analyze, and model data
Conduct exploratory data analysis to identify patterns, trends, anomalies, risks, and opportunities
Support the development and maintenance of scalable data pipelines and ETL/ELT processes
Work with structured and unstructured data from APIs, cloud platforms, databases, and other sources
Integrate analytical and predictive outputs into client-ready dashboards, reports, and tools
Build and maintain dashboards and data visualizations using platforms such as Power BI, Tableau, or Looker
Assist with evaluating model performance, data quality, and the accuracy of analytical outputs
Translate technical findings into clear business insights and recommendations for non-technical audiences
Support client meetings and presentations by preparing analyses, visualizations, and key takeaways
Conduct ad hoc analyses to answer specific client and business questions
Document methodologies, code, models, and project deliverables
Participate in code reviews and follow established standards and best practices
Support the responsible and effective use of AI across analytics workflows
Collaborate with data scientists, analysts, engineers, and strategists across multiple projects

Experience That Contributes To Success

1–2 years of experience in data science, data analytics, data engineering, business intelligence, or a related field, including relevant internship or professional experience
Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Mathematics, Economics, Engineering, or another quantitative discipline, or equivalent relevant experience
Hands-on experience using Python and SQL for data manipulation, analysis, and modeling
Familiarity with Python data science libraries such as pandas, NumPy, and scikit-learn
Foundational understanding of predictive modeling, statistical analysis, machine learning, and forecasting
Exposure to analytical techniques such as regression, classification, clustering, optimization, or time-series analysis
Experience with dashboarding and data visualization tools such as Tableau, Power BI, or Looker
Familiarity with ETL/ELT processes, APIs, relational databases, and data pipelines
Exposure to cloud data platforms such as AWS or Redshift is a plus
Foundational understanding of data modeling concepts, including star and snowflake schemas
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with close attention to detail
Ability to communicate technical concepts and analytical findings clearly to non-technical audiences
Ability to manage priorities and contribute across multiple projects in a collaborative environment
Experience in PR, communications, advertising, marketing analytics, or another client-service environment is a plus
Curiosity and a strong desire to continue developing technical, business, and client-facing skills
Commitment to using data and AI thoughtfully, responsibly, and effectively

Burson is an equal opportunity employer and considers applicants for all positions without discrimination or regard to particular characteristics. We are committed to fostering a culture of respect in which everyone feels they belong and has the same opportunities to progress in their careers.

Individual compensation varies based on job-related factors, including location, business needs, level of responsibility, experience, and qualifications. We offer a competitive benefits package; click here for more details: https://mybenefits.wpp.com/public/welcome.

The base salary for this position at the time of this posting may range between:

$35,000—$75,000 USD

You Belong At Burson

Our vision is for Burson to be the leading ‘academy company’ for creative communications professionals and emerging leaders. We provide a dynamic environment where ambitious colleagues come to elevate their skills, expand their networks, and ultimately, produce the best solutions for today’s leading brands. Our commitment to your growth is reflected in our robust benefits and people programs, which include professional development opportunities, mentorship programs with industry leaders, a vibrant and inclusive company culture fostering collaboration and innovation and packages designed to reward and retain top talent. We invest in our people because we believe their success is our success.

At Burson, we’re an agency of learn-it-alls. We recognize that the things we do best, creativity and communications, require a level of nuanced understanding. That’s why it’s imperative for us to hire extraordinarily talented people of all backgrounds and identities. Without that we can’t do the essential work of inspiring bold ideas, fostering constructive dialogue, cultivating meaningful experiences, and driving innovation and creativity for our partners. Your unique point of view—your talent—is what makes you a #BursonPerson, and it’s how we deliver exceptional results for our clients, together.

jobs.description:
Title

CAD Drafter (Temporary)

Job type

Temporary, three to four months, non-exempt, hourly
Full-time (8 hours per day)

Location(s)

Colorado Springs, CO (Remote/Hybrid Considered)

Overview

PteroDynamics is seeking a detail-oriented Temporary CAD Drafter to support our manufacturing team during a 3 - 4 month assignment. In this role, you'll create and update engineering drawings, technical illustrations, and manufacturing documentation that support the production of our innovative Transwing® aircraft systems.

This is an opportunity to contribute to a fast-moving aerospace startup, working closely with engineers and technicians to turn designs and shop-floor feedback into accurate, production-ready documentation.

The position is based in Colorado Springs, CO, with remote or hybrid arrangements considered based on experience and project needs. This position is expected to work 40 hours per week.

About Us

PteroDynamics Inc. designs superior autonomous vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) aircraft systems that fly faster and go farther to reach remote locations without runways, even in harsh conditions. PteroDynamics’ Transwing® aircraft is unlike any other VTOL system, performing like a great fixed-wing aircraft with superb VTOL capabilities.

Transwing aircraft unfold their wings to transition smoothly and quickly between vertical and horizontal flight, overcoming limitations inherent in other VTOL designs by combining fixed-wing aircraft speed, range, and endurance with superior VTOL performance in an efficient, highly automated platform. The Transwing is ideal for automating time-sensitive delivery of critical high-value payloads to hard-to-reach locations, including maritime logistics support, payload delivery to remote locations without airstrips, and reconnaissance and surveillance.

Seeing is believing. Visit www.PteroDynamics.com for details and videos.

Description

As a Temporary CAD Drafter, you'll play an important role in supporting our engineering and manufacturing operations by preparing detailed technical drawings, assembly illustrations, and documentation used throughout the manufacturing process.

You'll work from CAD models, sketches, engineering redlines, and manufacturing feedback to develop clear, accurate drawings and technical packages. This role requires strong attention to detail, the ability to manage multiple priorities, and a practical understanding of how engineering drawings translate into physical hardware.

We're looking for someone who can work independently, collaborate effectively with technical teams, and deliver quality work within established project timelines.

Key Responsibilities

Create and revise engineering drawings for parts, assemblies, tooling, fixtures, and manufacturing applications.
Prepare production-ready drawing packages using CAD models, sketches, redlines, and engineering inputs.
Develop technical illustrations, exploded views, assembly details, and documentation for standard work instructions.
Incorporate engineering changes, manufacturing feedback, and as-built updates into existing drawings.
Apply appropriate dimensions, tolerances, section views, notes, and parts callouts to technical drawings.
Collaborate with design engineers, manufacturing engineers, and technicians to clarify design requirements and resolve drawing discrepancies.
Provide timely drawing revisions and technical illustrations to support ongoing manufacturing and assembly activities.
Maintain drawing accuracy, revision histories, and organized technical documentation.
Support drawing release, configuration management, and document control processes.
Identify and help resolve inconsistencies between drawings, CAD models, bills of materials, work instructions, and physical hardware.
Assist with standardizing drawing templates, symbols, notes, and drafting practices.
Support the development of manufacturing work instructions, inspection aids, and other technical documentation.

Required Qualifications

Minimum of one year of professional experience in drafting, design documentation, or a related engineering or manufacturing environment.
Experience creating and revising engineering drawings for parts, assemblies, tooling, or manufacturing processes.
Proficiency with CAD or drafting software used to develop production drawings and technical documentation.
Ability to interpret 3D models, sketches, engineering redlines, and technical inputs to produce accurate drawings.
Working knowledge of engineering drawing conventions, including dimensions, tolerances, section views, detail views, notes, and revision control.
Ability to create clear technical illustrations and manufacturing documentation.
Strong attention to detail with a commitment to accuracy and consistency.
Effective written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate with engineers and technicians.
Ability to work independently, prioritize assignments, and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
U.S. Citizenship or Permanent Resident Status required.
Ability to collaborate effectively with a team based in Colorado Springs, CO.

Preferred Qualifications

Familiarity with ASME Y14.5 standards and geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T).
Experience in aerospace, unmanned aircraft systems (UAS), composites, automotive, defense, or other complex hardware environments.
Hands-on experience in manufacturing, prototyping, assembly, inspection, maintenance, or related technical work.
Experience developing exploded views, assembly illustrations, standard work instructions, or other technical illustrations.
Familiarity with product lifecycle management (PLM), product data management (PDM), document control, and engineering change processes.
Experience collaborating directly with machinists, technicians, and engineers to resolve technical drawing questions.
Demonstrated ability to balance accuracy and efficiency while managing multiple priorities in a fast-moving environment.

Our Values

Our values guide how we work with one another, support our customers, and solve challenging problems:
People: We value relationships with our colleagues and customers while embracing and upholding the worth of every individual.
Excellence: We have a mindset of excellence at all times.
Accountability: We believe the foundation of trust is accountability
Knowledge: We believe that innovation and success depend on gaining, documenting and sharing knowledge

Salary range

$20.00 - $36.00 per hour, depending upon experience.

What We Offer

At PteroDynamics, you will have the opportunity to significantly impact the future of aerial technology through creativity and innovation. PteroDynamics offers eligible employees a comprehensive compensation and benefits package, which includes competitive compensation, stock options, company-sponsored medical insurance, dental, vision, life insurance, a 401(k) plan with company matching, long-term disability, paid time off, paid holidays, and paid sick time. All employees enjoy a collaborative, inclusive working environment in an exciting, growing startup company.

Note

This job posting in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the employee(s) incumbent in this position. Employees will be required to follow any other job-related instructions and perform any other job-related duties requested by anyone authorized to give instructions or assignments.

We prohibit unlawful discrimination against applicants or employees on the basis of age 40 and over, color, disability, gender identity, genetic information, military or veteran status, national origin, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, or any other status protected by state or local law.

jobs.description:
Research Associate, NGS Laboratory

Start November 2026, contract-to-hire

What you’d be doing

Crownlands builds large patient-centric datasets that help us explore biology, discover new medicines, and improve human health. In our laboratory in South San Francisco, we create this data on massive scale, and you would be one of the people making that happen. You’d run automated prep, check quality, and load sequencing runs. This is hands-on work in a production lab. You’d work alongside other RAs, scientists, and the automation engineers who build our systems. You can earn the opportunity to contribute to our operating system and convert to a full-time position.

Responsibilities

Accessioning samples, tracking them by barcode, and setting up plates
Running and overseeing automated protocols
Preparing NGS libraries across several protocols, and helping take new kits from first run to production-scale
Running and maintaining liquid handlers and other instruments
QC’ing samples and libraries, and flagging anything out of spec
Noticing where a workflow is fragile or a QC checkpoint is missing, and telling us

Role requirements

A bachelor’s in molecular biology, biochemistry, genomics, bioengineering, or a related field, or equivalent lab experience
At least a year of practical experience in lab work
Lab fundamentals: pipetting, nucleic acid extraction, sample prep, enzymatic assays
Exposure or interest in liquid handlers or 96/384-well plate workflows
Strong organizational skills and good habits around documentation and sample tracking
U.S. citizenship or work authorization for the length of the contract

Nice to have

Experience with the following: Liquid handlers; NGS library prep; automated extraction and magnetic bead cleanups; QC instruments like Qubit, Microplate Reader, Fragment Analyzer, or QuantStudio; LIMS or barcode-based sample tracking.
Hands-on experience in a high-throughput genomics, sequencing, or diagnostics lab

You don’t need experience with every instrument on this list. If your fundamentals are strong and you want to learn automation, we’ll teach you.

Physical requirements and work environment

Ability to stand and walk for extended periods, up to 6 hours during an 8-hour shift, while performing laboratory operations.
Ability to lift, carry, and move laboratory supplies, equipment, and materials weighing up to 25 lbs (11 kg) occasionally.
Ability to perform repetitive hand movements and fine motor tasks, including pipetting, sample handling, and operating laboratory instruments.
Ability to bend, reach, and move between laboratory workstations and equipment as required.
Ability to work in a laboratory environment while following established safety procedures and wearing appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE).

Pathfinder Oncology, Inc. (PFO) - pathfinderoncology.com - is a dynamic oncology company headquartered in Chapel Hill, North Carolina. Our thesis is that long-term, exceptional outcomes in metastatic cancer require the activation and harnessing of anti-tumor immunity.

We partner directly with patients, pairing a concierge-style care model with highly tailored, often first-of-their-kind treatments: bespoke mRNA and peptide vaccines built from tumor-specific genomic and proteomic profiles, personalized TCR-T cell therapies, and pathway-based regimens. Our team spans drug development, multi-omics interpretation, and compassionate patient care.

Position Summary

The Bioinformatics Operations & Genomics Analyst is responsible for executing PFO’s patient-specific projects, coupling high scientific standards and urgency. The role owns the path from a vendor's raw data delivery to a reviewed, reportable result that will impact the patient treatment strategy: data in the door with its provenance intact, established immunogenomics workflows run against a clinical clock, every output reviewed before it informs a design decision, and results turned into the reports on which the company acts.

No two cases arrive the same way, so the work is operational without being routine. This is not a methods-development role, and not a pipeline-babysitting one. The central skill is judgment: knowing what a good result looks like and stopping a bad one before it reaches a physician. The second is leverage: using automation and AI agents to carry many concurrent cases without dropping any.

Key Responsibilities

Data Operations

Own intake for WES/WGS, RNA-seq, and single-cell deliveries — transfer, checksum verification, provenance, and registration in PFO's data ledger. Maintain per-patient tracking so every result traces to the reads that produced it, and manage storage lifecycle, cost, and access.

Pipeline Execution

Run PFO's immunogenomics workflows on cloud infrastructure: alignment, QC, somatic calling, copy number and purity, expression, HLA typing, and neoantigen prediction. Resolve job failures and keep configurations, reference bundles, and container versions pinned so any case reproduces exactly, months later, by someone else.

jobs.description:
Remote | United States | Project-Based Independent Contractor 

Compensation
: $35-$40 USD/hour, based on relevant experience and project requirements 

Help Shape the Future of AI in Government 

What if your years of experience navigating government regulations, evaluating complex cases, or interpreting public-sector policies could help make artificial intelligence more accurate, reliable, and effective? 
At Volga Partners, we're bringing experienced government professionals into the next generation of AI development. 
We're seeking Government Subject Matter Experts (SMEs)
who can apply their professional knowledge, analytical judgment, and industry experience to evaluate and improve advanced AI models. 
This isn't a traditional government position, and you won't be processing applications or managing government caseloads. Instead, you'll use your expertise to assess how well AI systems interpret information, apply regulations, reason through complex scenarios, and produce accurate, defensible conclusions. 
Your expertise is what matters. AI experience is a plus, not a requirement. 

The Opportunity 

As a Government SME, you'll serve as a subject matter evaluator, helping assess the quality, accuracy, and reasoning of AI-generated responses across specialized government functions. 
You'll examine realistic scenarios, identify errors or gaps in AI-generated conclusions, and provide expert feedback grounded in established regulations, policies, and professional standards. 
Your contributions will help improve how AI systems understand and respond to complex public-sector challenges. 

Areas of Expertise We're Seeking 

We're particularly interested in professionals with substantial knowledge and practical experience in one or more of these areas: 
1. Government Policy, Public Records & Regulatory Compliance 

Interpreting federal, state, or local government regulations and policies 

Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), public records, and disclosure requirements 

Privacy compliance, sensitive information protection, and regulatory auditing 

Evaluating complex compliance scenarios and identifying regulatory risks 

2. Government Programs, Eligibility & Administrative Decision-Making 

Interpreting government program requirements and eligibility regulations 

Evaluating complex cases, supporting documentation, and administrative determinations 

Identifying inconsistencies, compliance issues, or unsupported decisions 

Applying professional judgment to regulatory and program-specific scenarios 

3. Government Procurement, Contracts & Vendor Evaluation 

Federal, state, or local government procurement processes 

Request for Proposal (RFP) analysis and evaluation 

Contracting standards, vendor selection, and procurement compliance 

Developing or applying evaluation criteria, scoring methodologies, and defensible recommendations 

You do not need expertise in every area. We're seeking depth of knowledge within your particular specialization.

What You'll Do 

Evaluate AI-generated responses: Review complex government-related scenarios for accuracy, completeness, reasoning, and regulatory alignment. 

Apply expert judgment: Determine whether AI-generated conclusions are appropriate, defensible, and supported by relevant policies or regulations. 

Identify errors and gaps: Recognize inaccurate interpretations, flawed assumptions, missing information, and potential compliance concerns. 

Validate against authoritative sources: Use applicable statutes, regulations, agency guidance, and professional standards to verify findings. 

Develop evaluation benchmarks: Help establish high-quality reference responses, assessment criteria, and examples of sound professional reasoning. 

Provide actionable feedback: Clearly explain your evaluations and recommend improvements to AI-generated content. 

Collaborate on quality: Apply project-specific evaluation guidelines and participate in quality reviews to support consistency and accuracy. 

Why Join Volga Partners? 

Put your professional expertise to work in a new way. 

Rather than performing traditional government administrative functions, you'll apply the knowledge you've developed throughout your career to emerging AI technology. 
Contribute to meaningful AI development. 

Your evaluations will help identify weaknesses in AI reasoning and improve the accuracy and reliability of AI-generated information. 
Work remotely with project-based flexibility. 

Participate in specialized assignments from anywhere in the United States, with opportunities for future engagements based on project availability and performance. 
No AI background required. 

We value professionals who understand their field and can recognize when an AI-generated answer is right, wrong, incomplete, or misleading. 

Project Details 

Engagement: Independent contractor, project-based 

Location: Remote, United States only 

Compensation: $35-$40 USD/hour 

Schedule: Variable, based on project assignments and deadlines; weekday or weekend availability may be needed 

Duration: Initial short-term pilot, with potential future project opportunities 

Selection Process: Qualified candidates must successfully complete a skills-based assessment evaluating domain expertise, analytical reasoning, and ability to follow project guidelines 

Hours and future assignments are not guaranteed. Compensation is subject to completion of assigned work in accordance with project instructions and quality standards. 

Ready to Apply Your Expertise to the Future of AI? 

If you've built your career understanding government systems, interpreting regulations, evaluating complex information, or making informed professional assessments, we'd love to hear from you. 

Bring your expertise. Help us build better AI. 

Apply today to be considered for upcoming Government SME opportunities with Volga Partners. 

Requirements

Who We're Looking For

We're seeking experienced professionals who bring more than familiarity with government processes. You should be comfortable analyzing complex information, exercising independent judgment, and explaining the reasoning behind your conclusions. 

Required Qualifications 

At least 2 years of relevant professional experience in government operations, public administration, regulatory compliance, government procurement, or a closely related field

Description

About Peregrine

Peregrine Advisors is a rapidly growing AI and data innovation hub helping government solve hard problems and deliver better outcomes. We work across the full lifecycle—from strategy and governance through architecture, engineering, analytics, AI, visualization, and training—for clients including the SEC, PCAOB, DDOT, and DCAA.

Our clients describe our support as “absolutely excellent” and our people as “instrumental to organization’s success.” Winner of the United Nations COP27 Datathon, our work has earned all Exceptional CPARS ratings, SEC Chair’s Awards, the SEC Vision Award, and recognition from FDA leadership.

We are also built differently. Peregrine is the first and only social enterprise organized as a Benefit Corporation and SBA 8(a) company focused on AI and data for government. We believe business success should create client value, social value, and opportunity for our people.

As we enter our next stage of growth, we need dependable, motivated, and skilled people who have a combination of intellectual curiosity and intellectual courage. With new clients, larger programs, and expanding responsibilities, the people joining Peregrine now will have the opportunity to help shape the company we become.

People first. Ownership always.

We solve problems through people, process, and technology—in that order. Technology matters, but people make transformation happen. That principle defines our culture. Trust and motivation are the foundational pillars of delivery on which our skills stand. We hire people we can trust, who care deeply about what they do, take ownership, learn quickly, help one another, and refuse to walk past a problem because it belongs to someone else.

At Peregrine, you are not joining simply to fill a position. You are joining a team, taking ownership of a mission, and helping build a company. If that excites you, we should talk.

At Peregrine Advisors, you will develop Python services on Amazon Web Services (AWS) that read and route federal filings automatically. But we hire people, not seats. As the work evolves, you will move to where the hardest problems are.

This is a hybrid work arrangement based in the Washington, DC metropolitan area, and the commuting cadence varies by assignment. The initial engagement requires United States citizenship and the ability to obtain a Public Trust determination.

Your first project

Your First Project Will Likely Have You Helping a Federal Agency Move a Manual, Paper-heavy Intake Process Onto An Intelligent Pipeline. Depending On The Assignment, You May

Develop cloud services in Python that read, interpret, and route a high-volume stream of filer applications.
Extract structure and meaning from filings at scale by combining optical character recognition (OCR) with AI.
Score each extraction for confidence and write the logic that decides where a document goes next.
Implement exact and fuzzy matching and the business rules that validate each submission.
Build human-review workflows for the decisions a machine should not make alone.

You help deliver an automated intake pipeline that takes filings from submission to decision at volume, in a setting where accuracy and auditability are not optional.

This is where you start, not the shape of your career here.

Requirements

4+ years of hands-on software development experience using Python
Bachelor's degree
Experience building cloud document-processing systems with Amazon Textract or an equivalent service, from OCR through extraction
Data validation experience, including exact and fuzzy matching
Experience with application programming interfaces (APIs) and SQL for moving documents through a processing workflow to a decision
Proficiency in writing, PowerPoint, and Excel

Preferred

Applied experience with large language models (LLMs), machine learning, or natural language processing (NLP)
Familiarity with Amazon Bedrock
PDF processing experience

Who you are

You have a hacker's mindset: you would rather ship a working prototype tonight than a perfect plan next week. You have built real document-processing systems in Python, and you move at the speed of the tools, not the clock. You experiment, fail, learn, and repeat quickly. You would rather own an outcome than be handed a task.

What you bring

Deep, practical Python skills and hands-on experience with cloud document processing on Amazon Textract or a comparable service, covering OCR through extraction.
The supporting engineering: validating data, matching records, and building the APIs and SQL that carry each document to a decision.
Sound judgment for building in a regulated environment where accuracy and auditability are not optional.

You adapt your development workflow as AI tools evolve, using them to help implement, test, and improve the components you own. You give the tools clear context, review and test their output, and remain accountable for the code you deliver.

When we talk

Be prepared to discuss a difficult problem you worked through, the decisions you made, what happened, and what you learned. The technical assessment is a live Python coding exercise.

Benefits

This is a full-time W-2 position with a salary of $92,000 to $133,000 per year.

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance with the employee premium fully paid and half of dependent premiums; employer-paid life, accidental death, and short-term and long-term disability insurance; a 401(k) matched 100% up to 4% of salary, vesting immediately; unlimited paid time off; and sponsored professional certifications and continuing education.

What we offer

You will work alongside developers, engineers, data scientists, architects, and strategists, on work ranging from strategy to implementation. We support your development across assignments and clients through extensive onboarding, sponsored professional certifications such as the Data Management Capability Assessment Model (DCAM) and AWS technical certifications, and rotation across functions to expand your skills and perspective. The mission is real, the problems are hard, and you own what you ship.

What we commit to

As a Benefit Corporation, our commitment runs three ways: real, measurable value for our clients; government that works better for the public; and a team that makes everyone in it better.

We hire people who want to help build the firm, not just work at it. If that is you, apply.

jobs.title: Kilo Lab Technician
jobs.description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.

Lilly recently announced a $4.5 billion investment to create the Lilly Medicine Foundry, a new center for advanced manufacturing and drug development. The first-ever facility of its kind, combining research and manufacturing in a single location, the Medicine Foundry will allow Lilly to further develop innovative solutions to optimize manufacturing processes and increase capacity for clinical trial medicines, while also reducing costs and environmental impact.

The Process Translation and Execution (PTE) team translates API/DS process knowledge into clinical supply readiness, oversees technology transfer, implements phase-appropriate control strategies, and ensures right-first-time clinical manufacturing for a variety of modalities, including synthetic molecules, biologics, peptides, oligonucleotides, and bioconjugates (ADC, ARC, etc.). Through cross-functional collaboration, PTE influences process design, revolutionizes clinical manufacturing, builds capabilities in emerging technologies, and aligns with corporate and Lilly Research Labs (LRL) goals, drives scientific excellence and innovation to accelerate manufacturing advancements, and propels the site toward long-term business success.

In the Foundry Construction and Project Delivery/Startup Phase (2025 to 2028), roles will be fluid and dynamic as we build a new organization, design and implement the necessary systems and business processes required to enable operational readiness, support project delivery, and build the site culture. Success will require significant collaboration, creativity, and resilience as the Lilly Medicine Foundry transitions from design to startup and ultimately to steady-state operations and continuous improvement. This period presents a unique opportunity for learning, growth, and making a lasting impact.

The Lilly Medicine Foundry Kilo Lab Technician actively supports start-up activities to bring manufacturing equipment into service. The Technician becomes an expert in their assigned area and supports the team on the proper operation of the facility. This role requires domestic and international travel to collaborate, train, and learn from sites that currently produce APIs. Upon completion of the project phase, the Technician provides on-the-floor support for production of API molecules, ensuring a safety-first, quality-always approach while executing a production process that encompasses diverse unit operations and manufacturing skills.

We are seeking passionate and agile technicians to join the PTE team and help bring the Lilly Medicine Foundry's vision to life.

Responsibilities

This role ensures the supply of our medicines by supporting the team, following instructions, assisting with troubleshooting, collaborating cross-functionally, and upholding our safety-first, quality-always mindset. The Kilo Lab Technician will be an integral part of executing the transfer of chemical processes from development laboratories to kiloscale operations, supporting clinical supply activities across multiple modalities including small molecules, peptides, oligonucleotides, and high-potent compounds. Technicians will support daily Kilo Lab activities to meet production plans by:

Adhering to compliance requirements (safety, quality, and environmental) and appropriately escalating any adverse events.
Operating processes and equipment according to batch records, user manuals, design parameters, standard operating procedures, and work instructions to meet the production schedule.
Conducting lab or pilot plant experiments, maintaining notebooks or records, and supplying written summaries to supervisors as needed.
Accurately dispensing materials as requested and executing written and verbal directions, including material testing, complex experimental designs, and/or process scaling up to pilot plant level.
Ensuring completion of daily monitoring, testing, and cleaning duties to keep equipment and systems in good operating condition per local and corporate regulatory requirements.
Assembling and disassembling machinery for processing of materials, demonstrating strong mechanical aptitude.
Serving as a cultural contributor to site safety culture, promoting compliant operations and positive safety behaviors.
Supporting troubleshooting and reaction to process upsets, integrating operator input and escalating as appropriate.
Following all applicable procedures for safety event reporting and documentation, including spill response, issue escalation, and initiating Emergency Response procedures as needed.
Ensuring adequate communication at shift changeovers and participating in daily shift huddles/meetings to understand and set expectations for daily operational goals.
Ensuring all area personnel follow cGMP practices, safe work habits, plant dress code, hygiene standards, and housekeeping requirements unique to the work area and job classification.
Summarizing, preparing, and tabulating data; coordinating activities with other laboratories and support groups.
Making interpretations of data generated and suggesting subsequent experimentation; offering ways to improve efficiency of time utilization, equipment design, configurations, and process improvements.
Planning own work schedule and operating with minimal supervision; level of independence increases with experience and equipment familiarity.
Actively participating in assigned building and area operations such as safety audits, procedure coordination, housekeeping, and continuous improvement projects.
Understanding and utilizing computer systems and programs for development project activities, including control or automation systems such as Delta V and Pi.
Using specified company-supplied personal protective equipment (PPE) (e.g., hair and beard coverings, lab coats or gowns, safety shoes, safety glasses, hard hats, etc.) as required.
Performing clean room gowning and wearing respirators and safety equipment during processing and cleaning of equipment/rooms.

Basic Qualifications

High School Diploma or GED required.
3+ years of direct manufacturing experience; GMP and/or chemical processing strongly preferred.
Demonstrated learning agility to operate a variety of new equipment and systems.
Strong mechanical aptitude and experience working with solvents and large equipment.
Demonstrated experience in manufacturing, cGMP, or a regulated environment.
Qualified applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Lilly does not anticipate providing sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H-1B, TN, or similar) for this position.

Additional Skills And Preferences

Previous experience in facility or area start-up environments.
Prior work in pharmaceutical or chemical manufacturing involving Process Safety Management regulations or hazardous chemicals.
Previous experience operating kiloscale glassware and equipment such as glass reactor systems, filtration equipment (AFDs, Nutsche filters, cartridge), rotary evaporators, and pumping systems.
Ability to work cross-functionally with PTE scientists, process engineers, operations, analytical chemists, safety and quality representatives.
Experience in small molecule, peptide/oligonucleotide, or high-potent manufacturing operations.
Familiarity with unit operations regarding distillation, filtration, extraction, and chromatography.
Solid understanding of FDA guidelines and cGMP requirements.
Demonstrated strong documentation skills.
Knowledge of lean manufacturing principles.
Problem-solving skills: proven ability to analyze data, perform root cause analysis, and resolve complex technical challenges.
Ability to understand technical nomenclature and language and work with mathematical formulas.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to handle and prioritize multiple projects and requests.
Demonstrated ability to manage priorities and ambiguity.
Demonstrated initiative to solve problems, troubleshoot issues, and learn new processes and computer system applications.
Ability to effectively communicate (electronically, written, and verbal) across levels and functions.
Basic computer skills required; proficiency in MS Word, Excel, and PowerPoint preferred.
Working knowledge of synthetic chemistry.
Post-secondary education helpful.
Highly motivated, able to learn rapidly, and demonstrates strong attention to detail.
Strong teamwork and interpersonal skills.
For internal Lilly employees - LRL/Product Research Development experience preferred

Other Information

This is a manufacturing-based role.
This position requires flexibility to work either first or second shift.
May be required to provide support outside of normal working hours, including nights or weekends.
Initial location: Lilly Technology Center – North (LTC-N), Indianapolis, IN.
Permanent location: Lilly Medicine Foundry, Lebanon, Indiana.
Limited domestic and international travel (< 10%) may be required. Potential exposure to chemicals, allergens, loud noises, and controlled substances.
Role requires ability to work in laboratory and manufacturing environments.

jobs.description:
Manufacturing Associate, DNA synthesis

At Ansa Biotechnologies
Emeryville, CA

Our mission at Ansa Biotechnologies is to revolutionize the way we make DNA. Compared to reading or editing life’s code, writing new code from scratch has remained one of the field’s most elusive challenges. At Ansa, we are putting nature to work, creating novel enzymatic solutions that will redefine how we build DNA. We believe that the biggest challenges our world faces will be solved using biotechnology and that DNA synthesis is the fuel for that transformation. Our enzyme-based approach (published in Nature Biotechnology) promises to dramatically accelerate innovation in biological research and biotechnology, including therapeutics, diagnostics, biomanufacturing, and synthetic biology. We look forward to our DNA products making an impact.

Currently hiring for swing shift Wednesday - Saturday. Hours are 3:30pm - 2:00am.

We believe lab automation facilitates novel synthetic biology applications through the synthesis of high-quality DNA at scale. In this role, you would accelerate the rate of discovery by developing and utilizing automated systems to dramatically impact synthetic biology. As one of the first members of our manufacturing team, you will have the opportunity to help build and support a growing and critical part of our operations. Beyond manufacturing, you will be a part of a dynamic, cross-functional, highly collaborative team operating at the interface between chemists, synthetic chemists, enzymologists, and automation experts.
If you have a passion for the life sciences and the fundamental components of new technology, this job is for you!

Responsibilities

Routinely start, purify and ship custom DNA oligonucleotide products using a novel enzymatic synthesis technology.
Leverage new protocols and implement into a rapidly scaling manufacturing pipeline working alongside a multidisciplinary team (manufacturing personnel, technology transfer & development departments).
Regular activities range from reagent and buffer preparation to cloning and cell culture purification work.
Operate using standard operating procedures (SOP) to execute a number of DNA synthesis equipment and sample traceability (LIMS) processes.
Work with teammates to design and scale next generation manufacturing systems for Ansas growing manufacturing platform.
Must be able to lift 50lbs and stand for long periods of time.
Collaborating in a team environment: At Ansa, communication between teams is critical–our technology is built on enzymes, chemistry, and automation. Additionally, we believe that honesty and openness are an instrumental part of the scientific endeavor.

Experience

Comprehensive knowledge of and experience with molecular cloning and bacterial cell culture gained through education or hands on industry experience.
Working knowledge of liquid handling robots (ie. Hamilton, Tecan, Agilent Bravo) and other similar high throughput manufacturing tools.
Experience following SOPs and directions for both simple and highly complex processes.
Ability to learn and adapt quickly in a multidisciplinary environment with tight deadlines and specifications.
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to clearly discuss and present technical concepts and results.
Commitment to demonstrating kindness, respect, and collaboration with a diverse set of colleagues of different backgrounds and disciplines.

What We Offer:

Competitive hourly pay and equity.
Generous benefits package including health, dental, and vision.
Ongoing professional development and training opportunities.
A collaborative and innovative work environment.
The opportunity to be part of a company at the forefront of synthetic biology and innovation.

jobs.title: Research Associate – Analytical Operations & QC Coordinator
jobs.description:
About Thintronics®

More Data. Faster.
Thintronics is solving one of the defining challenges in modern computing: moving massive amounts of data and power between chips at unprecedented speeds and densities. As Moore's Law slows, performance is increasingly defined by advanced packaging, chiplets, and high-density substrates. Our materials technology enables new levels of interconnect density, signal integrity, and power delivery inside next-generation semiconductor packages. We partner directly with leading IDMs, foundries, substrate manufacturers, and OSATs building the most advanced AI and HPC platforms in the world.

Thintronics is a start-up company located in Alameda, CA. We are a team of chemists, materials scientists, and engineers shaping the future of data and devices. We offer an exciting start-up environment at the interface of R&D, machine learning-aided product design, manufacturing, and rapid market implementation.

Job Role – Who We Want

Thintronics is looking for a detail-oriented and highly organized Research Associate to keep our Analytical Intelligence for Materials (AIM) Team running smoothly and reliably. This role owns the operational backbone of the analytical lab: sample intake and tracking, instrument scheduling and calibration/maintenance, quality control on measurement data, and documentation/recordkeeping standards. You'll ensure that the physical characterization work happening in the lab (thermal, mechanical, and dielectric testing) is consistent, well-documented, and audit ready, so the broader team can trust the data driving product decisions and QC of manufactured rolls.

This is a great fit for someone who thrives on structure, process, and follow-through rather than open-ended experimentation. We are looking for someone who gets satisfaction from a well-run lab, clean data, and nothing falling through the cracks. As part of a start-up team, you will wear many hats, and while there is meaningful hands-on lab work involved (50-70% of time), the core value you add is consistency, rigor, and operational reliability. This role is collaborative both within the AIM team and cross-functionally across Thintronics. Specific duties may evolve based on the needs of our quickly growing company as well as your skillset/interests.

Core Responsibilities

Coordinate sample intake and tracking across analytical testing pipeline
Schedule, calibrate, and maintain instrumentation
Establish and enforce QC checks on experimental data and test results
Maintain and improve SOPs, recordkeeping systems, and documentation standards for lab operations
Partner with cross-functional teams to prioritize testing queues and manage turnaround times

jobs.title: Life Science Research Professional 1
jobs.description:
Job Description

Stanford University is seeking a Life Science Research Professional 1 to perform basic functions and activities involved in defined research projects, and independently conduct and analyze experiments.

The Department of Pathology is a founding department of the Stanford School of Medicine and one of the leading departments in the United States. Our preeminent faculty spans from emerging leaders to highly accomplished physicians and scientists, including a Nobel laureate and members of the National Academy. Our mission is to improve the diagnosis, treatment, and basic understanding of human disease. This is done through discovery (research), education, and clinical care.

You will be working with an unparalleled leading-edge community of faculty and staff that are fundamentally changing the world of health care. You will have the opportunity to influence and drive change with your innovative ideas, the ability to make a difference, and participate in human advancements. Our culture is fast-paced, energetic, and growing all of the time.

We offer a variety of benefits beyond traditional medical, dental, retirement, and savings options:

Events and programs for children, sports camps, tuition options
World-class intellectual stimulation through learning and development classes, workshops, and onsite conferences from leading-edge speakers and faculty
Work/life and family-friendly policies and reimbursement
Participation in Stanford’s social responsibility and sustainable programs for a better world
A vibrant university culture that values the uniqueness of each individual

We are seeking candidates who are progressive thinkers, see challenges as simply problems to solve, and have the spirit and energy to change the world.

About The Department Of Pathology

Comprised of extraordinary faculty and staff, our mission is to improve the ability to diagnose, treat, and understand the origin and manifestation of human disease, and to care for those who have or are at risk of developing diseases. We accomplish this through our clinical services (in all fields of anatomic and clinical pathology, including molecular and genomic pathology, histocompatibility testing and transfusion medicine) and research (which includes basic, translational and clinical research into the origins and manifestations of disease, including efforts to improve disease prediction and prevention as part of the goal of achieving precision medicine and health), and also by educating future leaders in pathology and related fields. Everything we do is to achieve the goals of providing the highest quality of clinical services to the patients for whom we passionately care, to advance our ability to understand, diagnose, monitor, and ultimately to cure disease or to prevent or delay its occurrence, and to provide outstanding education and career development opportunities to those who share these goals.

For more information about the department visit http://pathology.stanford.edu/

About The Lab

The Svensson Lab in the Department of Pathology at Stanford University School of Medicine discovers new hormones and signaling pathways that control metabolism and translates them into therapies for obesity, type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and cancer. The lab combines peptide biochemistry, cell signaling, gene editing, computational prediction, and mouse physiology to define how secreted peptides act on cells, tissues, and whole organisms. Recent discoveries include a brain-derived peptide that suppresses appetite and obesity independently of the incretin pathway (Nature, 2025). A growing focus of the lab is how GLP-1-based drugs such as semaglutide, now used by millions of people, affect cancer development and growth. The lab is part of the Stanford Diabetes Research Center and works with collaborators at Stanford and internationally.

About The Position

We are seeking a Life Science Research Professional 1 (LSRP 1) to join the group of Dr. Katrin Svensson in the Department of Pathology to study GLP-1 in cancer. Under the supervision of the PI, the LSRP 1 will assist with planning, perform, and analyze cellular experiments and peptide bioactivity assays and will support in vivo cancer studies involving semaglutide treatment. The LSRP 1 will analyze and interpret experimental results, discuss potential follow-up studies with the PI, prepare figures and abstracts, and contribute to presentations and manuscripts under the guidance of the PI or senior researcher. This is an excellent opportunity for a motivated scientist seeking substantial hands-on research experience at the intersection of metabolism and cancer.

Desired Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in biology, biochemistry, molecular and cell biology, cancer biology, physiology, pharmacology, bioengineering, or a closely related life science field.
At least 1 year of hands-on research laboratory experience (academic or industry); research experience in cancer biology, metabolism, or pharmacology is a plus.
Interest in analyzing and graphing quantitative data and applying basic statistics (e.g., GraphPad Prism, Excel); familiarity with R or Python is desirable.
Interest in preparing scientific figures, abstracts, or presentations; interest in presenting at scientific conferences.
Proficiency with dilutions, molarity, and other standard laboratory calculations.
Ability to interpret results, troubleshoot experiments, and propose follow-up experiments based on project needs and their assigned work, with review and guidance from the PI or senior researcher.
Strong organizational and record-keeping skills; ability to manage several experiments in parallel and meet deadlines.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills and ability to work collaboratively in a team.
Willingness to work with mice and to complete required animal-care training.

Physical Requirements*:

Frequently stand, walk, twist, bend, stoop, squat, grasp lightly, use fine manipulation, grasp forcefully, perform desk-based computer tasks, use telephone, write by hand, lift, carry, push and pull objects weighing over 40 pounds.
Occasionally sit, kneel, crawl, reach and work above shoulders, sort and file paperwork or parts.
Rarely climb, scrub, sweep, mop, chop and mix or operate hand and foot controls.
Must have correctable vision to perform duties of the job.
Ability to bend, squat, kneel, stand, reach above shoulder level, and move on hard surfaces for up to eight hours.
Ability to lift heavy objects weighing up to 50 pounds.
Ability to work in a dusty, dirty, and odorous environment.
Position may require repetitive motion.
Consistent with its obligations under the law, the University will provide reasonable accommodation to any employee with a disability who requires accommodation to perform the essential functions of his or her job.

Working Conditions

May require working in close proximity to blood-borne pathogens.
May require work in an environment where animals are used for teaching and research.
Position may at times require the employee to work with or be in areas where hazardous materials and/or infectious diseases are present.
Employee must perform tasks that require the use of personal protective equipment, such as safety glasses and shoes, protective clothing and gloves, and possibly a respirator.
May require extended or unusual work hours based on research requirements and business needs.
Due to the nature of the work, this position will be fully on-site.

Responsibilities

Core Duties
:

Plan approach to experiments in support of research projects in lab and/or field based on knowledge of scientific theory.
Independently conduct experiments; maintain detailed records of experiments and outcomes.
Apply the theories and methods of a life science discipline to interpret and perform analyses of experiment results; offer suggestions regarding modifications to procedures and protocols in collaboration with senior researcher.
Review literature on an ongoing basis to remain current with new procedures and apply learnings to related research.
Contribute to publication of findings as needed. Participate in the preparation of written documents, including procedures, presentations, and proposals.
Help with general lab maintenance as needed; maintain lab stock, manage chemical inventory and safety records, and provide general lab support as needed.
Assist with orientation and training of new staff or students on lab procedures or techniques.

Minimum Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree in related scientific field.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

General understanding of scientific principles. Demonstrated performance to use knowledge and skills when needed.
Demonstrated ability to apply theoretical knowledge of science principals to problem solve work.
Ability to maintain detailed records of experiments and outcomes.
General computer skills and ability to quickly learn and master computer programs, databases, and scientific applications.
Ability to work under deadlines with general guidance.
Excellent organizational skills and demonstrated ability to accurately complete detailed work.

jobs.title: Customer Success Manager, Beneficial Deployments - Life Sciences
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

Join Anthropic as a Customer Success Manager for Life Sciences. You’ll be a strategic partner and trusted advisor to leading organizations working to accelerate scientific discovery, such as research institutes, academic medical centers, and scientific foundations. You’ll help these organizations harness the full potential of Claude through deep product expertise, use case discovery, and hands-on guidance.

You’ll be part of a Research and Life Sciences account team pod, working as one team with your Account Executive and Applied AI partners. Together you’ll shape account strategy with you taking the lead on adoption, change management, and value realization.

This role doesn’t follow a single playbook. You’ll run a range of Customer Success motions, from deep 1:1 strategic partnership to one-to-many programs like webinars, hackathons, and cohort-based enablement. You’ll choose the motion based on top account and customer priorities and the best way to solve for them.

The insights you gather will directly inform our research priorities, product development (including how Claude for Life Sciences evolves), and strategies for beneficial AI deployment. That makes you a key voice in how we build and deliver AI systems that accelerate science for the benefit of society.

Responsibilities

Build trusting, strategic relationships with research leaders, scientists, principal investigators, and program directors to understand their scientific priorities, organizational goals, and impact objectives
Partner closely with your Account Executive and Applied AI counterparts in the Research and Life Sciences pod on shared account plans, bringing in Product, Support, and other teams as needed
Run the right Customer Success motion for each account and customer priority, whether that’s dedicated 1:1 engagement, cohort-based onboarding, hackathons and build days, office hours, or researcher communities
Become an expert in Anthropic’s products, especially Claude for Science, guiding organizations and their researchers and scientists to the right solutions and most impactful use cases
Monitor usage patterns and proactively drive adoption, identifying optimization opportunities and new applications for Claude across your book of business
Develop and execute change management strategies suited to scientific and academic cultures, including Train the Trainer programs, Center of Excellence development, and enablement that respects partner capacity, governance requirements, and decision-making processes
Guide partners through the technical and governance foundation for launch, including SSO and provisioning, workspace configuration, and data handling considerations for research and health data (such as HIPAA, IRB, and institutional data policies)
Own account and success plans and run Quarterly Impact Reviews that document and quantify value realized, such as research productivity, time-to-insight, and cost savings, and partner with Marketing on success stories and reference accounts
Establish the repeatable playbooks, templates, and health metrics that define what “great” looks like for customer success in life sciences at Anthropic

You may be a good fit if you have

6+ years of experience in Customer Success, Technical Account Management, Solutions Engineering, or consulting
3+ years of experience in life sciences research, with exposure to new technologies as a catalyst for accelerating progress
Experience working directly with life sciences organizations, such as academic research institutions, research institutes, foundations, biotech, or pharma, and familiarity with how scientific research is conducted, funded, and governed
An understanding of the regulatory, risk, and compliance needs of the industry
Experience driving success across both consumption-based and seat-based business models, with an understanding of the expansion levers and success metrics for each
Experience managing dedicated strategic accounts and delivering one-to-many programs, with the judgment to choose the right motion for the customer priority at hand
Strong cross-functional collaboration skills, including working as part of an account team with Sales and technical partners and advocating effectively for customer needs
Technical fluency in AI/ML concepts, API integrations, and software implementation patterns, and the ability to explain them to audiences ranging from bench scientists and computational researchers to institutional leadership. Familiarity with scientific data types, research workflows, or bioinformatics tooling is a strong plus
A data-driven, AI-first way of working, using adoption signals to guide decisions and building Claude-powered workflows into how you engage partners
Passion for both AI and accelerating scientific progress, with a strong interest in ensuring frontier AI systems are developed safely, ethically, and deployed to benefit society
A knack for bringing order to chaos and an enthusiastic “roll up your sleeves” mentality. You are a true team player

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary

$200,000—$265,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Application Close Date

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight! 

This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.

Blue Origin is building the next generation of orbital launch infrastructure, and the Western Range is where our next chapter gets written. A launch site is a lot more than a pad: it's roads, utilities, water and power, port and wharf access, integration and support facilities, and the connective tissue that lets the whole operation run. This is a civil engineering role for someone who wants to own that connective tissue from the front end, walking candidate ground, finding the constraints before they find you, shaping the conceptual design, and driving the early coordination with the agencies and A/E partners who will decide how it gets built.

You'll own civil planning and conceptual site design for the operational infrastructure that stands up a launch site. You'll build the early site layouts, surface the geotech and hydrology and environmental issues before they turn into schedule, and set the technical direction the A/E takes into design development.

This is not a construction-management seat. Most of what you touch isn't under construction yet. The decisions you're making are the ones that lock in what construction will look like two years from now, and the decisions that are hardest to walk back once the design catches up to them.

We're Looking For Someone Who

Treats a site walk as a chance to learn something the desk version can't show you
Is comfortable making decisions with incomplete information, then refining as the picture clears
Has been through enough of a design cycle to know where the hard problems hide
Wants to be in the room when we decide where everything goes and how it all talks to each other

Lead civil planning and conceptual site design for launch site operational infrastructure: roads, utilities, drainage, port and wharf access, integration and support facilities, laydown and staging, and the civil scope that ties them together
Support site evaluation and due diligence. Walk the ground, evaluate constraints (geotechnical, hydrology, flood, environmental, utilities, access), and build the case for or against candidate layouts
Drive early coordination with A/E partners. Shape technical scope, set direction, review schematic and design-development deliverables, resolve cross-discipline conflicts at the stage where they're cheap to resolve

Use BIM workflows to keep site and facility design coordinated across disciplines
Identify project risks early, surface them, and drive them to closure
Be in the field when the field needs you: site walks, agency meetings, early construction observation as projects progress

Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering or related engineering discipline
3+ years of professional experience in civil engineering design, planning, or site development (grading, drainage, utilities, roadways)
Proficiency in AutoCAD Civil 3D

EIT certificate or Professional Engineer (PE) license, or actively pursuing
Experience with site identification, due diligence, or front-end planning for aerospace, industrial, defense, or other heavy infrastructure projects

Experience with marine or port infrastructure (wharfs, docks, shore facilities, dredging coordination)
BIM software fluency (Autodesk BIM 360 / Construction Cloud, Navisworks, Revit)
Hydraulic and hydrologic modeling (ICPR, WaterGEMS, or similar)

Experience with California-specific environmental regulations or coastal engineering

That means making Claude the go-to tool for the life sciences ecosystem from early discovery in academia to paradigm shifting biotech to reimaging pharma pipelines — and building the technical infrastructure to back that up.

You'll work directly with flagship research partners like Howard Hughes Medical Institute and The Allen Institute, embedded in their scientific workflows. This isn't consulting from the outside — you'll be building alongside their engineers, prototyping agents that fit into real research pipelines, and developing the ecosystem-level tooling (MCP servers, benchmarks, reusable agent skills) that extends Claude's usefulness across the broader life sciences community. This role will be part of the founding Beneficial Deployments applied AI team focused on bringing more of life sciences closer to the frontier and be responsible for building with our partners.

Responsibilities

Partner deeply with flagship life sciences research institutions — understand their scientific workflows end-to-end, build hands-on with their engineering teams, and help take projects from early exploration to production systems integrated into how they do science day-to-day.
Develop reusable ecosystem infrastructure, like MCP servers for domain-specific data sources (genomics platforms, literature databases, experimental repositories), instruments, scientifically-grounded benchmarks, and agent skills that other institutions can adopt without starting from scratch.
Identify what's actually hard about deploying AI in life sciences (heterogeneous data, auditability requirements, the prototype-to-trust gap) and feed those findings back to product, engineering, and research.
Create technical content and documentation that lets partners self-serve, so what works for one institution can scale globally without the same level of hand-holding.

Deep research experience in life sciences, biomedical research, or scientific computing. Bonus if you've studied genomics, neuroscience, or drug discovery specifically and are comfortable getting deeply technical with academics.
Experience building LLM-powered tools or applications: prompting, context engineering, agent architectures, evaluation frameworks.
Builder credibility from shipping production code as a software engineer, forward-deployed engineer, or technical founder.
A scrappy mentality–comfortable wearing multiple hats, building from scratch, driving clarity in ambiguous situations, and doing whatever it takes to further the mission.
