jobs.description:
Application Close Date

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight! 

This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.

Blue Origin is building the next generation of orbital launch infrastructure, and the Western Range is where our next chapter gets written. A launch site is a lot more than a pad: it's roads, utilities, water and power, port and wharf access, integration and support facilities, and the connective tissue that lets the whole operation run. This is a civil engineering role for someone who wants to own that connective tissue from the front end, walking candidate ground, finding the constraints before they find you, shaping the conceptual design, and driving the early coordination with the agencies and A/E partners who will decide how it gets built.

You'll own civil planning and conceptual site design for the operational infrastructure that stands up a launch site. You'll build the early site layouts, surface the geotech and hydrology and environmental issues before they turn into schedule, and set the technical direction the A/E takes into design development.

This is not a construction-management seat. Most of what you touch isn't under construction yet. The decisions you're making are the ones that lock in what construction will look like two years from now, and the decisions that are hardest to walk back once the design catches up to them.

We're Looking For Someone Who

Treats a site walk as a chance to learn something the desk version can't show you
Is comfortable making decisions with incomplete information, then refining as the picture clears
Has been through enough of a design cycle to know where the hard problems hide
Wants to be in the room when we decide where everything goes and how it all talks to each other

Key Responsibilities

Lead civil planning and conceptual site design for launch site operational infrastructure: roads, utilities, drainage, port and wharf access, integration and support facilities, laydown and staging, and the civil scope that ties them together
Support site evaluation and due diligence. Walk the ground, evaluate constraints (geotechnical, hydrology, flood, environmental, utilities, access), and build the case for or against candidate layouts
Drive early coordination with A/E partners. Shape technical scope, set direction, review schematic and design-development deliverables, resolve cross-discipline conflicts at the stage where they're cheap to resolve
Support environmental planning and regulatory compliance: NEPA Environmental Assessments, environmental surveys, impact analyses, agency coordination (Space Force, FAA, state and local jurisdictions)
Produce sketch-level and spot-check civil design in AutoCAD Civil 3D to support fast turns on tie-ins, feasibility studies, and alternatives analysis
Coordinate with adjacent disciplines (structural, mechanical, electrical, fluids, geotech) to keep the multi-disciplinary picture coherent as the design matures
Help develop statements of work and technical scope for civil design, planning, and site evaluation activities
Use BIM workflows to keep site and facility design coordinated across disciplines
Identify project risks early, surface them, and drive them to closure
Be in the field when the field needs you: site walks, agency meetings, early construction observation as projects progress

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering or related engineering discipline
3+ years of professional experience in civil engineering design, planning, or site development (grading, drainage, utilities, roadways)
Proficiency in AutoCAD Civil 3D
Willingness to travel to candidate and active sites: frequent day trips and the occasional longer stint
Strong communication: written, verbal, and the kind where you have to make the case for a site decision to a room that doesn't start out agreeing
Comfortable rapidly changing roles and priorities in a high-paced, ambiguous environment
Must be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident (current Green Card holder)
Ability to obtain and maintain badging at government installations (Vandenberg SFB)
Ability to perform hands-on field work in heat, cold, rain, tight quarters, or at heights

Preferred Qualifications

Direct experience working at or with Vandenberg SFB, Western Range operations, or 30th Space Wing / Space Launch Delta 30 coordination
EIT certificate or Professional Engineer (PE) license, or actively pursuing
Experience with site identification, due diligence, or front-end planning for aerospace, industrial, defense, or other heavy infrastructure projects
Owner's-rep experience: sitting on the sponsor side of A/E design contracts, driving deliverables from concept through schematic
Working knowledge of adjacent disciplines (electrical, geotechnical, structural, surveying, piping) sufficient to spot when something doesn't add up at the interface
Experience with marine or port infrastructure (wharfs, docks, shore facilities, dredging coordination)
BIM software fluency (Autodesk BIM 360 / Construction Cloud, Navisworks, Revit)
Hydraulic and hydrologic modeling (ICPR, WaterGEMS, or similar)
Experience supporting NEPA and environmental regulatory research, preparation, and reporting
Familiarity with permitting and land-use coordination with government agencies (state, federal, military)
Experience with California-specific environmental regulations or coastal engineering

Base Pay Range For

CA applicants is $99,201.00 - $138,880.35

Other Site Ranges May Differ

Culture Statement

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical

jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

Anthropic's business metrics change quickly. New models, products and pricing land every few weeks, and each one moves the numbers in ways leadership needs to understand and act on quickly.

The Finance Analytics & Business Intelligence team is hiring a senior individual contributor to own how finance leadership reviews key business metrics. You'll run the weekly company metrics update and forum, explain what is driving revenue and usage across products, customers and models, and turn open-ended business questions into clear, data-driven answers. You'll also build what makes those answers repeatable and scalable: governed metric definitions, executive dashboards, and Claude-powered workflows for recurring analysis. The work is technical, fast-moving and highly visible, and it spans Finance, Product, Go-to-Market, Data Science and Data Engineering.

In This Role, You Will

Own the weekly company metrics update and forum: shape the story the numbers tell, evolve the structure and content as fast as the business changes
Define the metrics that matter: help establish the headline KPIs leadership uses to track the business, and the driver views beneath them.
Surface macro trends: explain what is driving growth across products, customers, and channels, and flag leading indicators early
Lead deep dives on executive questions: take a broad question from leadership, put a measurement approach around it, and work with partner teams to deliver a clear, defensible answer
Track performance against plan: explain where actuals differ from forecast and why it matters
Partner across teams: work with finance leadership, product and GTM finance and strategy, data science, and data engineering to agree on how we measure the business, so everyone uses the same numbers.
Raise the bar: land narratives in executive forums and up-level the team’s finance analytics practice by example

Have run an executive metrics forum: you've owned a recurring business review for senior leadership, including its structure, content and discussion.
Land narratives with executives: your analyses have changed business decisions, and you can simplify for senior leaders without losing rigor
Put shape around ambiguity: you’ve personally defined the measurement approach for questions nobody knew how to answer, without waiting for a fully specified ask
Stay hands-on at senior scope: you still write the SQL and Python yourself, and you’d rather ship a defensible v1 with honest error bars than wait for perfect data
Are inherently curious: you go one level deeper than asked and are energized by how fast models, products, and the market are moving
Thrive amid shifting priorities: you juggle multiple fast-moving work streams and stay effective when the plan changes weekly
Work fluently with modern tooling: you’re strong at data visualization, use Claude and AI tools as force multipliers in analysis and BI, and can self-serve your own workflows across SQL, Python, dbt, and a cloud warehouse

Significant experience in finance analytics, business analytics or data science, including direct partnership with senior leadership

Cloud platform experience (AWS, GCP) with orchestration, CI/CD for data, and testing/observability

jobs.title: Research Scientist, Life Sciences (Chemistry)
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

Anthropic's Life Sciences team is building a research group focused on biological discoveries by combining AI with hands-on biological research. We're seeking research scientists with deep medicinal chemistry expertise to join the team. Our goal is to speed up progress in the life sciences by an order of magnitude, and this role puts that mission into practice. You'll be an expert medicinal chemist with hands-on experience designing, synthesizing, purifying, and characterizing small molecules. Above all, you'll close the loop between AI-generated hypotheses and experimental data to share with the community. Working alongside AI researchers and engineers, you'll drive experimental programs end to end and pressure-test AI-designed molecules and AI-proposed synthetic routes against real chemistry.

This role is fully on-site in the San Francisco Bay Area.

Key responsibilities

Design multi-step synthetic routes for small molecules and oversee their execution end to end, including route selection, reaction optimization, purification strategy, and interpretation of full characterization data (NMR, LC-MS, HPLC)
Coordinate synthesis and biological evaluation with external contract research organizations and academic partners
Evaluate AI-designed molecules and AI-proposed synthetic routes, drive them to experimental readout, and feed results back to research teams
Apply medicinal chemistry principles, including SAR analysis and physicochemical property optimization, to compound design and prioritization
Ensure experimental data across programs is high quality and well documented, including procedures, spectra, and failure modes
Communicate findings clearly to chemistry, AI research, and life sciences audiences

Minimum Qualifications

PhD in chemistry
Demonstrated medicinal chemistry experience, including SAR-driven design and optimization of small molecules, with recent, sustained hands-on synthetic work
Comfort navigating ambiguity and defining problems in a rapidly evolving research environment
Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across cross-functional teams, with strong written and verbal communication skills

Preferred Qualifications

5+ years of medicinal chemistry experience beyond the PhD
Track record of advancing programs from hit identification through lead optimization
Experience directing synthetic chemistry activities at contract research organizations
Computational chemistry, cheminformatics, or coding skills, for example Python with RDKit or pandas for data analysis and automation
Experience using AI or ML tools in the life sciences
Publications and/or patents demonstrating scientific impact

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary

$300,000—$320,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.title: Biology Expert
jobs.description:
Biologists to build the life science scenarios frontier AI labs use to test model judgment. AfterQuery builds the expert evaluation data that frontier AI labs use to measure and improve their models. We're hiring biologists as contractors to author and grade the life science scenarios those evaluations run on. This is the anchor listing for our life, physical, and social science domain, and every biology specialty is welcome here. What you'll actually do

Author realistic biology scenarios from experimental design through interpretation, the kind a working scientist actually reasons through. Write reference answers with the scientific reasoning behind each conclusion, mechanisms and evidence weighed. Grade model output for mechanistic accuracy, evidence handling, and appropriate uncertainty. Flag explanations that read fluent but get the biology wrong, the misses only a trained scientist would catch.

Who this is for

Biologists with an advanced degree or equivalent research experience across any specialty, genetics, ecology, microbiology, physiology, evolution, and beyond. Researchers, industry scientists, and educators with at least two years of professional experience in the life sciences. Scientists who reason from mechanism and evidence, not from textbook summaries. People with strong written English who can turn scientific judgment into clear, teachable reasoning.

Contract and pay

$60 to $120/hr, paid weekly via Stripe. Your rate is set from your experience, not negotiated down after you start. Fully remote, fully async. No fixed hours. Minimum 10 hours per week, no maximum. Scale up or down week to week. No screen recording, no keystroke monitoring, no idle timers. Independent contractor. Ongoing project work rather than single task batches.

How our hiring process works

Apply at /apply/biology-expert. About five minutes. Resume plus a few structured questions. Resume review. Every application gets read against a published rubric and gets a decision. Written assessment. You may be asked to take a written assessment for further placement. Onboarding. Sign the contractor agreement, connect Stripe, and get platform access. Project match. You're matched to live work in your specialty, usually within a week of onboarding.

About AfterQuery

AfterQuery is an expert data lab. We build the evaluation and training data that frontier AI labs use to measure what their models can and can't do in real professional work. Our contributors are practicing professionals, not annotators, and the work is credited, reviewed, and paid at professional rates.

Responsibilities

Author realistic biology scenarios from experimental design through interpretation
Write reference answers with the scientific reasoning behind each conclusion
Grade model output for mechanistic accuracy and evidence handling
Flag explanations that read fluent but get the biology wrong

Required Qualifications

Advanced degree in biology or a closely related field, or equivalent research experience
2+ years of research, industry, or teaching experience in the life sciences
Depth in a biology area such as genetics, ecology, microbiology, or physiology
Clear written English for documenting scientific reasoning
Able to commit at least 10 hours per week

Preferred Qualifications

PhD and peer reviewed publications
Wet lab or field research experience
Teaching or science communication experience

Design and develop autonomous, multi-step, and tool-using AI agents using AWS Bedrock and agentic AI frameworks.

Looking to join a passionate team dedicated to developing and manufacturing life-saving biopharmaceuticals? Avid Bioservices is a leading clinical and commercial biologics CDMO focused on creating innovative solutions to meet the needs of our clients and improve patient outcomes.

Your Role:

The Senior Research Associate, Process Development Downstream
will provide laboratory support for Process Development by leading in the downstream process and/or method development. The Senior Research Associate may be assigned various tasks within the department and outside the department as needed.

Key Responsibilities:

Serve as a subject matter expert (SME) and/or technical lead for downstream process development and purification of monoclonal antibodies, recombinant proteins, and related biologics. Responsibilities include buffer formulation and preparation, chromatography process development and optimization, filtration development, and routine process execution.
Lead downstream process development studies, including chromatography screening, process optimization, and scale-up activities to support client programs from early development through commercialization.
Perform and oversee in-process and routine analytical testing to support downstream development activities, including protein concentration determination (A280), HPLC-based assays, and other relevant analytical methods.
Independently execute downstream unit operations using chromatography systems, filtration equipment, and associated process analytical tools with minimal supervision.
Support process scale-up, technology transfer, and manufacturing operations by developing robust buffer preparation strategies and downstream processing workflows suitable for pilot and GMP manufacturing environments.
Compile, analyze, interpret, and present experimental data. Author technical reports, development summaries, protocols, and client-facing documentation, and present findings during internal project reviews and client meetings.
Lead troubleshooting and continuous improvement initiatives to enhance process performance, robustness, productivity, and scalability.
Contribute to the evaluation, implementation, and validation of emerging technologies, process analytics, laboratory automation platforms, and process intensification strategies to improve development efficiency.
Experience with laboratory automation, process intensification, process analytical technologies (PAT), high-throughput process development, and data analytics is highly desirable.
Mentor junior scientists and provide technical guidance across downstream process development activities.
Perform other duties and project-related responsibilities as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree with 3-4 years of relevant biopharmaceutical industry experience, or a Master's degree in Chemical Engineering, Biochemical Engineering, Biotechnology, Biological Sciences, or a related field.
Candidates should possess a strong understanding of downstream processing principles, experimental design, data analysis, and bioprocess development methodologies.

Position Type/Expected Hours of Work:

jobs.description:
About Us

The people of Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSK) are united by a singular mission: ending cancer for life. Our specialized care teams provide personalized, compassionate, expert care to patients of all ages. Informed by basic research done at our Sloan Kettering Institute, scientists across MSK collaborate to conduct innovative translational and clinical research that is driving a revolution in our understanding of cancer as a disease and improving the ability to prevent, diagnose, and treat it. MSK is dedicated to training the next generation of scientists and clinicians, who go on to pursue our mission at MSK and around the globe.

Exciting opportunity at MSK: Join our Integrated Genomics Operation (IGO)
as a Research Assistant
! The Integrated Genomics Operation (IGO)
enables basic, clinical and translational research projects across the Cancer Center. Ultimately, the focus of our work is to help establish the basis of cancer pathogenesis, diagnostics and treatment at MSKCC. At the IGO, we implement the MSK mission to cure cancer by providing a broad range of genomic services and expertise to our world-class research scientists. We are a high-throughput core facility producing >100TB of data per year across >40 applications, including “fourth generation” genomics technologies such as single cell and spatial transcriptomics.

You will master a variety of genomics assays utilizing either robotics or traditional benchwork; and will interface with other teams within the IGO. As a full-service genomics lab, we provide high level expertise to the scientists and physicians at our institution.

Role Overview

Extract nucleic acids from a variety of biomaterial (fresh frozen and formalin-fixed paraffin embedded tissue, cell line, blood, plasma, serum, saliva, nails, etc).
Perform quality assurance and quality control of extracted material.
Train on cutting-edge spatial transcriptomic methods from 10x genomics platforms.
Learn the theory, design and execution of droplet digital PCR experiments, traditionally used to validate oncogenic alterations with a high degree of sensitivity and accuracy.
Work with your team to create a workflow following LEAN principles.
Communicate with vendor technical support and sales representatives.
Operate liquid handlers and robotic instruments for high-throughput processing.
Maintain accurate and detailed records in a Laboratory Information Management System (Examplar Sapio LIMS).
Use iLAB for billing purposes.

Key Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in biology, chemistry, or related field with at least 2 years of experience or Master’s degree.
Previous exposure to purifying nucleic acids for NGS platforms, knowledge of digital PCR, and experience with cells and FFPE samples is highly valued.

Core Skills

Exceptional attention to detail and strong analytical skills.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced research environment, managing multiple projects while maintaining precision. Enthusiastic about learning opportunities in the lab.
Critical thinking and problem-solving skills to troubleshoot experimental challenges.
Outstanding interpersonal and communication skills and the ability to interact across all levels in a confident, concise, and professional manner.
Comfortable with manual or automated processing.
Enthusiasm and dedication to MSK's vision, mission, and values.

Location: NYC
Schedule: Onsite, Monday to Friday

jobs.description:
Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline and portfolio of medicines to treat heart disease, obesity and obesity-related conditions, rare diseases, inflammatory conditions and cancer. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

Civil Engineer

What You Will Do

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this vital role you will provide technical leadership and engineering expertise for the planning, design, renovation, and delivery of civil and structural infrastructure supporting facilities, utilities, and capital projects. This role ensures designs are safe, compliant, constructible, reliable, and aligned with operational, business, and site requirements.

The Project Engineer partners with engineering disciplines, architects, project managers, facilities teams, EHS professionals, contractors, and external design firms throughout the project lifecycle. This position requires travel to project sites and organizational locations to support project development, design reviews, field assessments, construction activities, commissioning, and stakeholder engagement.

Serve as the technical lead for civil and structural engineering requirements, design standards, specifications, and project execution.
Develop and review civil and structural design criteria, calculations, drawings, specifications, scopes of work, and engineering studies.
Support projects involving site development, grading, drainage, stormwater management, roads, parking areas, underground utilities, foundations, structural steel, concrete, and building modifications.
Evaluate existing site and structural conditions; identify constraints, risks, and required remediation or reinforcement measures.
Review engineering design packages for technical quality, code compliance, constructability, maintainability, safety, and alignment with project requirements.
Coordinate with architectural, mechanical, electrical, process, environmental, and facility engineering disciplines to ensure integrated project solutions.
Lead technical aspects of capital projects from feasibility and concept development through detailed design, construction, commissioning, and turnover.
Travel as needed to support site assessments, project meetings, design workshops, construction reviews, inspections, commissioning, and operational-readiness activities.
Provide technical support during construction, including field observations, resolution of design issues, review of contractor submittals, and evaluation of change requests.
Ensure projects comply with applicable building codes, structural standards, civil design requirements, permitting obligations, and environmental regulations.
Support the development and maintenance of civil and structural engineering standards, specifications, guidelines, and standard details.
Identify design risks, recommend practical mitigations, and support risk assessments associated with facility modifications, infrastructure reliability, and site conditions.
Support commissioning and turnover activities to confirm civil and structural systems meet intended-use and operational requirements.
Monitor industry practices, codes, standards, and emerging technologies; incorporate relevant improvements into engineering standards and project delivery practices.
Provide technical mentoring and subject matter support to project teams and less-experienced engineers.

What We Expect Of You

We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The professional we seek is a leader with these qualifications.

Doctorate degree

OR

Master’s degree and 2 years of civil engineering, structural engineering, or a related engineering experience

OR

Bachelor’s degree and 4 years of civil engineering, structural engineering, or a related engineering experience

Associate’s degree and 8 years of civil engineering, structural engineering, or a related engineering experience

OR

High school diploma / GED and 10 years of civil engineering, structural engineering, or a related engineering experience

Preferred Qualifications:

Professional Engineer (PE) license in civil or structural engineering.
Advanced degree in civil engineering, structural engineering, or a related discipline.
Experience supporting industrial, manufacturing, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, research, or other regulated facility environments.
Experience with structural assessments, seismic evaluations, existing-building modifications, and infrastructure renewal projects.
Familiarity with stormwater management, site permitting, geotechnical engineering, and construction-phase engineering support.
Experience with relevant engineering software for structural analysis, civil design, or site-development planning.

What you can expect from us

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.

jobs.description:

Standard (Mon-Fri)

Environmental Conditions

Office

When you’re part of the team at Thermo Fisher Scientific, you’ll do important work, like helping customers find cures for cancer, protecting the environment, or making sure our food is safe. Your work will have real-world impact, and you’ll be supported in achieving your career goals.

As the world leader in serving science, we empower our people to advance innovative technologies, develop meaningful solutions, and build rewarding careers. With revenues of $45 billion and the largest investment in R&D in the industry, we give our 130,000 extraordinary minds the resources and opportunities to make significant contributions to the world.

The Materials and Structural Analysis Division’s Electron Microscopy business enables customers to find meaningful answers to questions that accelerate breakthrough discoveries, increase productivity, and ultimately change the world. The MSD EM business designs, manufactures, and supports the broadest range of high-performance microscopy workflows that provide images and answers in the micro-, nano-, and picometer scales.

Combining hardware and software expertise in electron, ion, and light microscopy with deep application knowledge in life sciences, materials science, electronics, and natural resources markets, our worldwide Electron Microscopy team is dedicated to supporting customers’ pursuit of discovery and solutions to global challenges.

Position Summary

The Senior Account Manager, Life Sciences Electron Microscopy is responsible for driving growth and managing strategic customer relationships across academic institutions, research universities, and core facilities within a defined territory including Southern California, Arizona, New Mexico, Nevada, Utah, and Colorado.

This role focuses on cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and volume electron microscopy (volume EM) solutions, partnering closely with leading researchers and facility directors to support advancements in structural biology, cryo-electron tomography, and 3D cellular imaging. The position plays a critical role in positioning Thermo Fisher Scientific as a trusted partner in cutting-edge academic research.

Responsibilities

The Account Manager is responsible for managing sales and account management activities for assigned academic accounts, defining and driving sales strategies, and ensuring achievement of bookings, revenue, and business goals.

Own all sales and account management responsibilities for Life Sciences Electron Microscopy solutions within academic institutions, national laboratories, and research centers across the assigned multi-state territory.
Focus on cryo-EM platforms, sample preparation workflows, and volume EM technologies supporting structural biology and advanced imaging research.
Develop and execute strategic account plans aligned to institutional priorities, grant funding cycles, and core facility growth initiatives.
Build strong relationships with principal investigators, lab managers, core facility directors, and university leadership across the region.
Identify, develop, and close opportunities across the full workflow, including instrumentation, automation, software, and service offerings.
Maintain accurate quarterly booking forecasts and provide regular updates to management.
Develop deep understanding of academic funding mechanisms, including federal grants (e.g., NIH), institutional funding, and shared instrumentation programs.
Confirm system configurations, specifications, and acceptance criteria to ensure successful order closure.
Partner with application scientists and product specialists to deliver technical demonstrations, workshops, and seminars tailored to academic audiences.
Drive adoption of advanced workflows such as single-particle analysis, cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET), and large-volume 3D imaging techniques (e.g., serial block-face SEM, FIB-SEM).
Support and grow user communities and core facility networks, including workshops, seminars, and user group activities across the territory.
Manage product evaluations and proof-of-concept engagements in collaboration with internal teams.
Coordinate with field service and support teams to ensure excellent customer satisfaction and long-term success.
Maintain continuous learning to stay current with rapid advancements in cryo-EM and volume EM technologies and academic research trends.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Life Sciences, Biochemistry, Structural Biology, Physics, Engineering, or a related field (advanced degree preferred).
Typically requires 5+ years of sales or account management experience in scientific instrumentation or related technologies.
Strong understanding of cryo-electron microscopy, structural biology, or advanced imaging workflows is highly desirable.
Experience working with or selling into academic or research environments.
Proven track record of managing complex capital equipment sales cycles.
Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to engage scientific audiences.
Strong problem-solving skills and ability to collaborate across cross-functional teams.
Ability to operate effectively in a highly matrixed organization.
Willingness to travel extensively across a multi-state territory (50% or more).

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting or selling cryo-EM, cryo-ET, or volume EM workflows.
Familiarity with academic core facilities and shared instrumentation models.
Experience engaging with grant-funded purchasing processes (e.g., NIH, NSF).
Miller-Heiman strategic and conceptual selling experience is highly desirable.
Ability to secure access to U.S. Government laboratories and facilities.

At Thermo Fisher Scientific, each one of our 130,000 extraordinary minds has a unique story to tell. Join us and contribute to our singular mission—enabling our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer.

Thermo Fisher Scientific is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin.

jobs.title: Senior Healthcare Data Analyst
jobs.description:
About the Opportunity

The Senior Healthcare Data Analyst is a full-time, senior individual contributor responsible for clinical, outcomes, and program analytics across the organization. Based in the United States, this role partners with clinical, operational, and executive leaders to turn complex questions into clear, meaningful insights.

The position requires an understanding of behavioral health care delivery across the patient journey, including referral, intake, admission, treatment, utilization, outcomes, and discharge. Additionally, this role helps advance AI-enabled analytical methods within the data analysis function, utilizing AI to enhance analytical speed, depth, and efficiency while establishing repeatable processes, independently validating outputs, and ensuring clinical and human oversight.

Key Responsibilities

Analyze access, conversion, census, capacity, utilization, length of stay, patient engagement, clinical outcomes, and program performance.
Develop an understanding of behavioral health care delivery, including intake, treatment planning, group, individual, and family therapy, psychiatry, documentation, authorization, outcomes, and discharge.
Partner with clinical and operational leaders to translate clinical workflows and complex operational questions into meaningful analyses, recommendations, and actionable insights.
Ensure analytical findings reflect actual care delivery workflows and are interpreted within appropriate clinical and operational contexts.
Identify trends, patterns, risks, and opportunities to improve care delivery, patient experience, and program performance.
Partner with clinical and research leaders to define research questions, outcome measures, analytical approaches, and data requirements for clinical studies and program evaluations.
Build accurate, well-documented, and reproducible datasets and analyses for outcomes research, program evaluations, presentations, abstracts, and publications.

Help Shape the Future of AI in Healthcare

What if your clinical expertise could help artificial intelligence better understand complex medical information, evaluate healthcare scenarios, and deliver more accurate, reliable responses?

At Volga Partners,
we’re connecting experienced healthcare professionals with opportunities to contribute to the development and evaluation of advanced AI models.

We’re seeking physicians, nurse practitioners, and physician assistants
who can apply their clinical knowledge, independent judgment, and evidence-based reasoning to evaluate AI-generated medical information.

This isn’t a traditional healthcare position. You won’t be providing direct patient care or managing a caseload. Instead, you’ll assess complex medical scenarios, challenge inaccurate conclusions, identify gaps in reasoning, and provide structured feedback that improves AI model performance.

Your clinical expertise is what matters. AI experience is a plus, not a requirement.

Important Note:
This is a freelance, task-based role designed for those seeking supplemental income. It’s essential to understand the nature of freelance work—tasks will be assigned as they become available, and work may be irregular or intermittent.

The Opportunity

As a Healthcare SME, you’ll serve as a subject matter evaluator, helping assess the quality, accuracy, and reasoning of AI-generated responses across specialized healthcare functions.

You’ll examine realistic scenarios, identify errors or gaps in AI-generated conclusions, and provide expert feedback grounded in established medical standards, clinical guidelines, and professional judgment.

Your contributions will help improve how AI systems understand and respond to complex healthcare challenges.

Areas of Expertise We're Seeking

We're particularly interested in professionals with substantial knowledge and practical experience in one or more of these areas:

General Practice

Physicians experienced in primary care, diagnostic assessment, preventive medicine, management of common medical conditions, and evidence-based clinical decision-making.

Family Medicine

Physicians with expertise in comprehensive primary care, acute and chronic disease management, differential diagnosis, and patient care across different age groups.

Internal Medicine

Physicians experienced in adult medicine, complex medical conditions, diagnostic interpretation, multisystem disease management, and evidence-based treatment decisions.

Nurse Practitioners (NPs)

Advanced-practice nursing professionals with experience in clinical assessment, diagnostic reasoning, treatment planning, patient management, and healthcare quality standards within their professional scope.

Physician Assistants / Physician Associates (PAs)

Qualified clinical professionals with experience in patient assessment, diagnostic evaluation, treatment planning, and interpretation of medical findings within their professional scope.

You do not need expertise in every area. We're seeking depth of knowledge within your particular specialization.

What You'll Do

Evaluate AI-generated medical content: Assess responses for clinical accuracy, completeness, relevance, and consistency with accepted medical standards.
Analyze clinical reasoning: Determine whether AI-generated assessments, differential diagnoses, and treatment recommendations are supported by appropriate clinical evidence.
Identify errors and inconsistencies: Recognize inaccurate medical information, unsupported conclusions, missing clinical considerations, and potential patient safety concerns.
Validate medical information: Reference authoritative medical literature, established clinical guidelines, and evidence-based healthcare practices.
Provide expert feedback: Clearly explain findings, identify opportunities for improvement, and recommend clinically appropriate corrections.
Support AI quality improvement: Apply established evaluation guidelines, scoring criteria, and project-specific quality standards.
Complete independent evaluations: Use designated online platforms to complete assignments accurately and within established project timelines.

Why Join Volga Partners?

Apply Your Clinical Expertise in a New Way

Use the medical knowledge and professional judgment you've developed throughout your career to contribute to advanced AI technology without providing direct patient care.

Help Improve AI Accuracy and Reliability

Your evaluations will help identify weaknesses in AI-generated medical information and support the development of more accurate, clinically informed AI systems.

Work Remotely

Participate in specialized project-based assignments from an eligible location, with schedules and workloads determined by project needs.

Explore the Future of Healthcare Technology

Gain experience contributing to advanced AI model evaluation while applying the professional expertise you already possess.

No AI Background Required

We're looking for strong clinical professionals who can recognize accurate medical reasoning, identify mistakes, and explain their assessments using sound professional judgment.

Compensation

Volga Partners offers project-based hourly compensation based on clinical specialization, relevant experience, professional qualifications, geographic location, and project requirements. See rates per expertise:

General Practice Physician: $75–$130

Family Medicine Physician: $85–$145

Internal Medicine Physician: $95–$160

Nurse Practitioner: $45–$85

Physician Assistant: $45–$85

Project Details

Engagement Type: Project-based independent contractor
Work Arrangement: Remote
Primary Location: United States
Additional Markets: United Kingdom, Australia, New Zealand, Canada, India, and the Philippines, subject to client approval
Schedule: Variable, including potential weekday and weekend assignments
Evaluation Platform: DataCompute
Project Duration: Based on client requirements and project availability
Selection Process: Qualified candidates may be required to complete a skills-based clinical evaluation assessment before selection

Specific assignments, schedules, workloads, and project dates will be communicated as they are confirmed. Hours and future assignments are not guaranteed.

Bring Your Medical Expertise to the Future of AI

If you're an experienced healthcare professional who enjoys analyzing complex medical information, applying evidence-based clinical judgment, and contributing to innovative technology, we'd love to hear from you.

Join Volga Partners and help shape the next generation of healthcare AI.

Apply today to be considered for upcoming project opportunities.

Recognized medical degree, advanced-practice qualification, or equivalent professional credential appropriate to the specialty and country.

Strong analytical, research, and problem-solving abilities.

Ability to work independently, follow detailed instructions, and meet established quality standards.

jobs.description:
About AtlasBase

AtlasBase is a fast-growing pioneer in Molecular Computing, bridging the gap between traditional IT and biotechnology. We are redefining global IT infrastructure by driving breakthroughs in both Molecular Compute and Molecular Data Storage. By commercializing synthetic DNA-based technologies at IT scale, AtlasBase delivers ultra-high-density, low-maintenance, and carbon-conscious solutions built for the explosive growth and value of the world's data. Leveraging nature’s most durable medium, we provide a virtually permanent foundation that transforms how the world processes and secures its most critical information.

Originally spun out of Twist Bioscience, our team is an elite fusion of scientists, engineers, and operators dedicated to solving some of the most complex infrastructure challenges on Earth. While our work is grounded in deep science, our success depends on world-class talent across every discipline. We are seeking a Research Associate, Surface Chemistry

who is ready to bring their expertise to a high-impact environment and help us build a brand-new category of technology.

About The Role

This is a unique opportunity to join a talented team of scientists and engineers focused on solving critical challenges in molecular data storage. As a Research Associate in surface chemistry, you will be primarily responsible for the surface modification and characterization of semiconductor substrates critical to our core technology. You will run day-to-day experiments to ensure the continuous supply of high-quality substrates for the broader team, while also developing and optimizing next-generation surface chemistry protocols. The ideal candidate is a rigorous and detail-oriented experimentalist with experience in surface metrology or functionalization and a passion for driving innovation in a highly interdisciplinary environment.

Responsibilities

Prepare, functionalize, and provide semiconductor substrates to the broader team for daily experimental workflows.
Develop and optimize novel surface chemistry and bioconjugation protocols to improve the performance and reliability of our high-density platforms.
Execute routine and advanced surface metrology to characterize substrates, including ellipsometry, contact angle measurements, AFM, and other relevant surface analysis techniques.
Process and analyze experimental data to guide surface chemistry optimization and troubleshoot technical issues.
Maintain detailed and meticulous records of all experimental work and analysis.
Effectively communicate experimental results, data analysis, and next steps to team members and leadership.
Act as a strong individual contributor while thriving in cross-functional collaborations with our synthesis, engineering, sequencing, and bioinformatics teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree with >2 years of relevant industry experience in Chemistry, Materials Science, Physics, Chemical Engineering, or a closely related field.
Deep, hands-on experience developing, optimizing, and executing surface chemistry protocols on solid substrates.
Demonstrated expertise in surface metrology techniques, including ellipsometry, contact angle goniometry, electrochemical characterization, and AFM.
Experience with bioconjugation and basic organic lab techniques is a plus.
Data analysis and scripting experience is highly desirable.
Experience in a biotech or pharma R&D environment is highly desirable.
Must be a creative and detail-oriented person with excellent analytical, verbal, and written communication skills.
Exceptional collaboration skills and ability to work seamlessly in a dynamic and fast-paced environment.

Physical Demands & Work Environment

Work will be performed onsite in office and laboratory space located in South San Francisco.
Mobility: Must be able to move about the laboratory and office environment regularly. This includes standing and walking for extended periods, often up to 6–8 hours per day.
Manual Dexterity: Must have fine motor skills and steady hands to handle delicate instruments, operate laboratory equipment, pipette accurately, and perform repetitive benchwork with precision.
Lifting/Carrying: Must be able to lift and carry up to 40 pounds occasionally, such as boxes of lab supplies or equipment.
Visual Acuity: Must have sufficient visual acuity to read small print on labels, instrument displays, and computer monitors. Close vision, color vision, and the ability to adjust focus are required.
Environmental Conditions: Frequently exposed to typical laboratory conditions, including biological samples, chemicals, and reagents. Must be able to wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) such as lab coats, gloves, and safety goggles as required.

80,000 - 110,000 USD per year(HQ)

The Global Analytics Business Consulting Team applies data science and AI to help customers turn commercial, medical, and regulatory data into action. We are seeking a Global Data Science Lead that will support execution of the Data Science AI strategy within this team. This role will lead a group of data scientists, AI/ML engineers, and analysts, and partners with Global Analytics leadership to turn strategy into delivery — applying advanced analytics, machine learning, and generative AI/LLM techniques to life sciences data.

Lead the Data Science function within the Global Analytics Team, in line with Veeva's Analytics Business Consulting goals

Collaborate with cross-functional consulting teams to understand customer business requirements and translate them into AI-native, data-driven solutions

Experience with the Life Sciences industry and applying analytics and AI/ML to related data sets

Advanced, in-depth specialization in data science and AI techniques including classification, pattern recognition, clustering, feature analysis, NLP, fuzzy matching, sentiment analysis, A/B testing, active/adaptive learning

jobs.title: Clinical Solutions Engineer (Subject Matter Expert) - West Coast
jobs.description:
Do you bring hands-on next-generation sequencing (NGS) experience and an understanding of clinical laboratory operations? Have you helped a clinical laboratory navigate CAP/CLIA requirements and bring a new assay into routine use? Do you want to utilise your technical and clinical knowledge within a commercialised environment?

If this sounds like you and you are driven by purpose, join the SOPHiA GENETICS NORAM Sales team as a Clinical Solutions Engineer and enable us to make a positive impact on the outcomes for cancer and rare disease patients worldwide.

This is a field-based role. You'll work from a home office or travel across your territory for customer meetings, conferences and events.

We're looking for someone based in the United States, in the region spanning the West Coast through Texas. In most instances, we look for individuals already living in-territory, but welcome those actively relocating to the area.

Our Mission

We believe there is a smarter, more data-driven way to make decisions in healthcare and our cloud-native AI powered SOPHiA DDM Platform makes that vision a reality on a daily basis. You will have direct input to our mission to democratize data-driven medicine for the ultimate benefit of cancer and rare disease patients across the globe.

Your Mission

You'll help clinical laboratories make informed decisions about purchasing the SOPHiA GENETICS ecosystem, drawing on your hands-on NGS experience and understanding of laboratory operations, assay implementation and CAP/CLIA requirements. Working alongside sales colleagues, you'll use that knowledge to understand customers' needs, address their concerns and explain what adoption would mean for their laboratory. Your role is to build confidence in the buying decision, not to carry out the implementation.

The value you add

Build credibility with laboratory teams by connecting to their clinical, technical and operational needs.
Help prospective customers assess what adoption would involve, using your knowledge of assay implementation, validation and the path to routine use.
Address buying concerns about CAP/CLIA requirements, documentation and implementation timelines with an understanding of how clinical laboratories work.
Partner with sales colleagues to answer technical and operational questions and help customers move towards a confident, informed buying decision.

Requirements

We know that every background is different, but to be best set for success we see you bringing:

Hands-on wet-lab experience with NGS workflows in a clinical laboratory.
An understanding of how clinical laboratories operate beyond the bench, including the steps needed to introduce and validate a new assay.
Substantial exposure to CAP/CLIA requirements and inspection processes, with enough involvement to explain their practical impact on laboratory work.
Experience of assay implementation or validation that helps you understand the challenges laboratories face before going live.
Willingness to travel for a customer-facing role.

You do not need to have held a customer-facing role, or previously worked as an SME or field applications specialist, but it is helpful. A desire to work in a commercialsed environment as part of a sales and solutions team is critical.

Benefits

You will be joining an organization with the patient at the heart of every decision and action, driven by purpose as we pursue exponential growth.

For more information about our Benefits, Virtues, The Recruitment Process, our AI guide and stories from our team about what it's like to work at SOPHiA, view the full posting on our careers page.

jobs.title: Manager, People Analytics & Data Science
jobs.description:
Position Summary

Mercury is building a connected, trusted people analytics capability that puts decision-ready data and insights in the hands of leaders when and where they need them. The Manager, People Analytics & Data Science will help build that capability from the data foundation through the leader experience.

This role will build reliable data pipelines and analytical datasets, establish trusted metric definitions, and deliver robust dashboards that enable self-service people data for Mercury leaders. The role will also conduct targeted research and advanced analysis—including predictive and AI-enabled methods where appropriate—to surface new insights on workforce risks, capacity, performance, productivity, and other priorities.

The successful candidate will combine technical depth with strong business judgment. They will be able to move from a business question to a data model, from a data model to a clear dashboard, and from an observed pattern to a well-supported recommendation. This is a builder role for someone who wants to make people data easier to trust, easier to use, and more useful in the flow of business decisions.

Geo-Salary Information

An in-person interview may be required during the hiring process

State specific pay scales for this role are as follows:

$128,136 to $252,194 (NJ, NY, WA, HI, AK, MD, CT, RI, MA)

$116,487 to $229,267 (NV, OR, AZ, CO, WY, TX, ND, MN, MO, IL, WI, FL, GA, MI, OH, VA, PA, DE, VT, NH, ME)

$104,839 to $206,340 (UT, ID, MT, NM, SD, NE, KS, OK, IA, AR, LA, MS, AL, TN, KY, IN, SC, NC, WV)

In CA: Typical hiring range is $171,148 to $209,181

The expected base salary for this position will vary depending on a number of factors, including relevant experience, skills and location.

Responsibilities

Data foundation and analytics engineering

Partner with data engineers to design, build, and maintain reliable data pipelines and analytical datasets that bring together people, organizational, operational, and business data from relevant sources.
Develop reusable data models, transformations, validation checks, documentation, and monitoring that support accurate and repeatable analysis.
Partner with HR Tech, Enterprise Data Science, Data & Analytics, Finance, and other technical teams on source systems, data architecture, integrations, access, and data quality.
Translate business and People questions into clear data requirements, grains, dimensions, logic, refresh expectations, and ownership.
Establish and maintain metric contracts that document definitions, calculation logic, sources, refresh cadence, interpretation, stewardship, and action path.
Improve the reliability, transparency, privacy, and usability of people data as Mercury evolves its HRIS and broader data ecosystem.

Dashboards and self-service people data

Own the end-to-end delivery of leader-facing people data products, from discovery and prioritization through launch, adoption, and iteration.
Build robust operational and executive dashboards that connect people metrics to business and workforce outcomes.
Deliver focused dashboard experiences that help leaders answer what changed, what may be contributing, and what action to take next.
Design for self-service by developing intuitive personas, access patterns, definitions, documentation, enablement, and feedback loops.
Embed relevant people insights into existing executive reporting and operating rhythms wherever possible rather than creating disconnected destinations.
Measure usage, trust, decision relevance, and adoption; use feedback and evidence to expand, refine, or retire products.

Research, advanced analytics, and predictive insight

Conduct targeted research and analysis on prioritized questions such as attrition risk, critical-role readiness, capacity constraints, workforce planning, manager effectiveness, performance, productivity, and AI-enabled work.
Apply exploratory analysis, statistical methods, experimentation, forecasting, segmentation, and predictive modeling as appropriate to the question and data quality.
Translate complex analysis into clear findings, limitations, implications, and recommendations for People and business leaders.
Design analyses with appropriate validation, explainability, privacy protections, and bias-awareness; treat models as decision support, not a substitute for accountable human judgment.
Develop repeatable approaches for research intake, hypothesis formation, analysis, peer review, storytelling, and follow-through.
Partner with stakeholders to connect analytical findings to decisions, interventions, and measures of impact.

Partnership and capability building

Build trusted relationships with People leaders, business leaders, Finance, HR Tech, Enterprise Data Science, and other partners.
Shape and maintain an analytics roadmap that balances foundational data work, self-service products, and targeted research.
Establish practical standards for data quality, versioning, testing, documentation, access, and responsible use of people data.
Help leaders and People partners build confidence and fluency in using people metrics and insights.
Lead through influence and contribute to a high-performing, collaborative People Ops, Tech & Analytics team.

What success looks like

Leaders can access trusted people metrics in the tools and business rhythms where decisions already happen.
Core dashboards are clear, adopted, well-governed, and connected to meaningful business questions.
Data pipelines, metric definitions, and analytical products are reliable enough to support recurring decisions—not just one-time requests.
Targeted research produces new, decision-relevant insight on priority workforce questions.
The team has a scalable roadmap for expanding self-service, predictive analysis, and future HRIS-enabled analytics.

Qualifications

Education

Bachelor’s degree in data science, statistics, computer science, mathematics, engineering, economics, business analytics, or a related field

Experience

7+ years of experience in data science, people analytics, analytics engineering, business intelligence, data engineering, or a related field.
Experience with People Analytics, HR data, workforce planning, talent, compensation, performance, or organizational research.
Demonstrated experience building data pipelines, analytical datasets, data models, or other reusable analytics infrastructure.
Demonstrated experience developing dashboards or self-service analytics products for business stakeholders.
Demonstrated experience applying statistical analysis, experimentation, forecasting, segmentation, or predictive modeling to complex business questions.
Demonstrated ability to communicate analytical findings clearly to senior leaders and non-technical audiences.
Strong hands-on skills with SQL and Python or R, plus experience with modern data pipelines, transformation, testing, and analytical workflows.
Experience with data modeling, semantic layers, BI tools, cloud data platforms, version control, and production-quality documentation.
Strong foundation in statistics, experimental design, causal reasoning, predictive modeling, and model evaluation.

Knowledge and Skills:

Able to distinguish between a reporting need, a diagnostic question, and a research or modeling question—and choose an appropriately rigorous solution.
Product-minded and user-centered: starts with the decision and designs the data experience around the user.
Strong storyteller who can make complex analysis clear, precise, and actionable without overstating certainty.
Highly collaborative, curious, pragmatic, and comfortable working across business and technical teams.
Strong judgment and discretion when handling confidential, sensitive, or personally identifiable People data.
Comfortable using AI and collaboration tools to improve productivity while applying responsible-use principles.
Able to build in ambiguity, establish standards without over-engineering, and continuously improve the quality of the work.

About The Company

Why choose a career at Mercury?

At Mercury, we have been guided by our purpose to help people reduce risk and overcome unexpected events for more than 60 years. We are one team with a common goal to help others. Everyone needs insurance and we can’t imagine a world without it.

Our team will encourage you to grow, make time to have fun, and work together to make great things happen. We embrace the strengths and values of each team member. We believe in having diverse perspectives where everyone is included, to serve customers from all walks of life.

We care about our people, and we mean it. We reward our talented professionals with a competitive salary, bonus potential, and a variety of benefits to help our team members reach their health, retirement, and professional goals.

Learn more about us here: https://www.mercuryinsurance.com/about/careers

Perks And Benefits

We offer many great benefits, including:

Competitive compensation
Flexibility to work from anywhere in the United States for most positions
Paid time off (vacation time, sick time, 9 paid Company holidays, volunteer hours)
Incentive bonus programs (potential for holiday bonus, referral bonus, and performance-based bonus)
Medical, dental, vision, life, and pet insurance
401 (k) retirement savings plan with company match
Engaging work environment
Promotional opportunities
Education assistance
Professional and personal development opportunities
Company recognition program
Health and wellbeing resources, including free mental wellbeing therapy/coaching sessions, child and eldercare resources, and more

May oversee multiple laboratories in a single department, or laboratories in multiple departments with a significant number of technicians. Highly specialized work may include development of research designs and fabrication, modification, repair, maintenance and operation of highly complex research or technical equipment.

Chief College Laboratory Technician

FLSA
Exempt

CAMPUS SPECIFIC INFORMATION
The Hunter-Bellevue School of Nursing at Hunter College is the flagship nursing school of the City University of New York (CUNY) and cultivates collaborative nurse leaders promoting wellness and championing health equity in local and global communities through excellence in education, research, scholarship, and advocacy. The School of Nursing invites highly motivated applicants for the position of Chief College Lab Technician.

Reporting to the Dean, the Chief College Lab Technician will:
•    Manage the day-to-day operations of the nursing labs, including scheduling, equipment maintenance, and inventory control.
•    Train and supervise lab personnel.
•    Enforce and implement safety protocols. 
•    Troubleshoot hardware and software issues and coordinates the maintenance and system upgrades of technology/equipment.
•    Support faculty and students in clinical teaching and simulation-based learning in nursing lab settings. 
•    Identify equipment and technology for clinical teaching and simulation-based learning.
•    Provide faculty training regarding technology and equipment.
•    Maintain currency and proficiency in related technology and software.
•    Ensure adherence to CUNY, state, and federal regulations for lab operations and safety.
•    Develop lab policies and procedures.
•    Work evenings and weekends as needed.
•    Other duties that align with the school’s mission and strategic goals.

High School Diploma with a minimum of twelve years' related experience. Additional education may be used to meet the experience requirement: an Associate degree may be substituted for two years experience, a Bachelor's degree may be substituted for four years experience, and a Master's degree in an area appropriate to the duties to be performed may be substituted for an additional one year's experience. This position requires a high level of technical expertise.

OTHER QUALIFICATIONS

•    Bachelor’s degree or higher in nursing.
•    New York State license as a registered nurse required or following hire. 
•    Experience in a nursing or simulation lab beneficial.
•    Strong knowledge of infection control, safety, and quality procedures.
•    Proficiency in nursing skills and technology.
•    Excellent organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills.
•    Expertise with Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint and other software systems.

Salary commensurate with education and experience ($102,508 - $111,459).

jobs.title: Data Engineer II- Life Sciences
jobs.description:
At H1, we believe access to the best healthcare information is a basic human right. Our mission is to provide a platform that can optimally inform every doctor interaction globally. This promotes health equity and builds needed trust in healthcare systems. To accomplish this, our teams harness the power of data and AI-technology to unlock groundbreaking medical insights and convert those insights into action that result in optimal patient outcomes and accelerates an equitable and inclusive drug development lifecycle. Visit h1.com to learn more about us.

As part of H1’s hiring process, all candidates are required to participate in an in-person final interview. Depending on your location, this may require travel.

H1's Data Network (H1DN) team is the client-data mastering network at the core of how H1's products get their data. We run production ingestion for major enterprise customers. Clinical trial data is one of our highest-visibility streams: it feeds decisions about where trials run and who runs them, and the people who depend on it are as often clinical experts as they are engineers. SLAs and customer expectations drive how we work, and we're looking for engineers who are energized by that.

What You'll Do At H1

As a Data Engineer II on the H1DN team, you will build and operate the pipelines behind H1's clinical trials data. You'll work primarily in Python, PySpark, and SQL, and you'll work directly with clinical subject matter experts and Customer Success Managers to turn their domain knowledge into pipeline logic that holds up in production.

You will:

Build and maintain the Python and PySpark pipelines behind the CTMS trial data pipeline intake workflows, including scoring and status logic.
Develop the transformation logic that maps raw trial and customer data to H1's internal data models, handling diverse source formats including CSV, JSON, Parquet, and APIs.
Write and tune SQL against large datasets to investigate data questions, validate pipeline output, and support analysis that clinical SMEs and customer-facing teams depend on.
Turn around customer-driven changes quickly, scoping requests as they arrive, shipping changes that hold up under enterprise SLAs, and reworking logic as customer needs shift mid-flight.
Partner with clinical SMEs to translate domain expertise into concrete data rules, then walk them through the results, explain what the pipeline did and why, and fold their feedback back into the logic.
Build the data quality checks, validation logic, and reconciliation that let non-engineers trust pipeline output without reading the code.
Participate in code reviews, maintaining a high bar for quality and adherence to engineering standards.
Monitor and improve pipeline observability, contributing to alerting and dashboards that surface job health and data anomalies for both the team and internal users.

About You

You are a data engineer with a strong Python foundation and real distributed-processing experience. You're drawn to high-impact teams where the work is tangible: pipelines running, enterprise customers getting their data on time, clinical data that people make real decisions from. You're comfortable in an environment where recurring production runs and customer SLAs shape day-to-day priorities, and where a customer request can reorder your week. You'd rather sit down with a domain expert and understand why the data looks the way it does than build to a spec handed to you secondhand.

You bring experience:

Building and shipping production data pipelines in Python, with an understanding of what makes them reliable and maintainable under real load
Working with PySpark or a comparable distributed processing framework on datasets too large for a single machine
Writing SQL well enough to answer hard questions about data, not just retrieve it
Working in an operationally-driven environment where reliability and on-time delivery matter as much as new feature work
Working directly with non-engineering partners, subject matter experts, analysts, or customer-facing teams, and communicating clearly about data with people who don't read code
Holding a high bar in code review and expecting the same from those who review your work
Identifying data problems early and seeing work through to resolution rather than handing it off

Requirements

3+ years of experience in software or data engineering, with meaningful Python in your background
Demonstrated experience building and maintaining production-grade data pipelines in Python
Hands-on experience with PySpark or a similar distributed data processing framework
Strong SQL skills, including working with large, messy, multi-source datasets
Strong understanding of software quality practices: testing, code review, documentation, and CI/CD
Experience working with cross-functional and non-technical stakeholders
Experience with pipeline orchestration tooling (Argo, Airflow, Databricks, dbt, or similar) preferred
Familiarity with clinical trial data, healthcare data, or another regulated data domain a plus
Familiarity with entity matching or data mastering a plus
Familiarity with AWS services (S3, Lambda, ECS, or similar) a plus

Compensation

This role pays $110,000 to $135,000 per year, based on experience, in addition to stock options.

Anticipated role close date: 10/20/2026

Full suite of health insurance options, in addition to generous paid time off
Pre-planned company-wide wellness holidays
Retirement options
Health & charitable donation stipends
