About the Company

Our client translates extraordinary science into everyday miracles, helping biotech, biopharma, and life sciences companies everywhere deliver novel vaccines, therapeutics, and diagnostics. We are global leaders in providing products and services within the fields of nucleic acid production and biologics safety testing to many of the world's leading biopharma, vaccine, diagnostics, and cell and gene therapy companies.

About the Role

Our client is seeking Temporary Manufacturing Associates I to support hands-on production operations across two manufacturing departments: Oligo Manufacturing and RNA Reagents Manufacturing. These are entry-level opportunities for individuals with a scientific background who enjoy working with laboratory equipment, preparing materials, following detailed procedures, and completing accurate production documentation.
Both assignments involve producing liquid products in a laboratory manufacturing environment. The Oligo role involves a more specialized, detailed production workflow focused on oligonucleotide synthesis and processing. The RNA Reagents role involves more general laboratory production, with additional responsibilities related to product inventory and stock management.

Key Responsibilities

Prepare materials, supplies, and equipment for daily production activities.
Follow established Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), safety guidelines, and quality requirements.
Perform hands-on laboratory production activities, following detailed instructions and established workflows.
Operate basic laboratory equipment, such as pipettes and centrifuges, and learn to use additional equipment as trained.
Accurately document production activities and maintain required records in accordance with company procedures.
Maintain clean, organized, and safe laboratory work areas.
Review production instructions, prepare materials, and support production workflows and changeovers as needed.
Recognize and report equipment issues, process deviations, or other concerns to the appropriate team member.
Complete required company, safety, quality, and role-specific training.
Collaborate closely with team members and supervisors to maintain production schedules and workflow.
Perform additional duties as assigned.

Department-Specific Responsibilities

Oligo Manufacturing :
Support the production of oligonucleotides through specialized laboratory manufacturing processes, including synthesis, purification, and processing under supervision. Follow detailed production sequences, prepare materials, operate laboratory equipment, and complete required documentation. This role requires a high level of attention to detail due to the more specialized production workflow.
RNA Reagents Manufacturing :
Support general laboratory production of RNA reagents and related products. Responsibilities may include preparing materials, performing laboratory procedures, supporting purification processes, maintaining product inventory, conducting cycle counts, ensuring supplies are stocked, and entering or retrieving information in an ERP system as trained.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in chemistry, Biochemistry, Biology, Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, or a related field; relevant equivalent experience may also be considered.
0–3 years of experience in a laboratory, biotech, life sciences, pharmaceutical, or manufacturing environment or relevant Degree. Candidates with experience in food production, barista work, or other high-volume procedure-driven environments may also be considered
Must have strong attention to detail, organization, and a commitment to accuracy and thorough documentation.
Ability to learn laboratory equipment, production processes, and new procedures.
Must have experience following SOPs, work instructions, safety procedures, or quality standards.
Must be eager to learn, and ability to work collaboratively with a team.
Comfortable working onsite in a laboratory environment for most of the workday and with a small team.
Ability to lift up to 50 pounds when needed and stand or walk for extended periods.
Must have excellent attention to detail: Follows procedures carefully and produces accurate work.
Organization: Keeps materials, equipment, and workspaces orderly.
Learning and growth: Desire to learn and grow within a laboratory, biotech, life sciences, pharmaceutical
Problem-solving: Recognizes basic issues and escalates concerns appropriately.
Accountability: Takes responsibility for following procedures and maintaining quality standards.
Coachability: Accepts feedback, learns from training, and applies instructions consistently.

Bonus Qualifications

Experience or ability in using basic laboratory equipment and performing hands-on laboratory procedures.
Oligo Manufacturing: Previous experience in biotech or life sciences manufacturing, particularly with oligonucleotides, nucleic acids, or similar laboratory production processes. Exposure to cGMP and ISO Class 7 or 8 cleanroom environments is a plus.
RNA Reagents Manufacturing: Previous experience in laboratory production, reagent preparation, or other process-driven laboratory operations. Familiarity with ERP systems, cycle counts, or purification processes is a plus but is not required.
Hands-on experience with pipetting either laboratory coursework, research, or professional experience.

Additional Information

Hands-on laboratory manufacturing assignments in San Diego/ Sorrento Valley area.
Both positions are entry-level and best suited for candidates with approximately 0–3 years of relevant experience or related education. Candidates with significantly more experience may be overqualified for the scope of the role.
A relevant scientific degree and hands-on pipetting experience are important for candidates without prior professional laboratory experience.
Candidates from food service or food production may be considered if they also have the necessary scientific education and laboratory skills. Food service experience alone is not sufficient.
Assembly and packaging backgrounds alone are not a fit because these positions involve producing liquid reagents rather than assembling or packaging finished products.
ERP systems, inventory procedures, specialized equipment, and department-specific production processes can be taught.
The first one to two weeks will generally focus on training, reviewing and signing off on SOPs, and shadowing team members.
Associates will work in laboratory attire while in the lab. Outside of lab, attire is very casual.

jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Research Associate supports daily operations in our CLIA/CAP-regulated clinical diagnostics laboratory. Responsibilities span hands-on wet-lab work (cell culture and assay support), clinical sample accessioning, chain-of-custody activities and customer-facing coordination. The role requires strong technical competence, meticulous documentation, and a service-oriented approach to maintain compliance, turnaround time, and quality.

Key Responsibilities

Clinical Laboratory Operations (CLIA/CAP)
·      Perform laboratory activities in accordance with CLIA, CAP, and laboratory SOPs, including documentation, data integrity, and change-control requirements.
·      Maintain accurate records in LIMS/ELN systems for samples, reagents, QC/QA activities, and test-related documentation.
·      Support internal audits, corrective and preventive actions (CAPA), and continuous improvement initiatives as assigned.
·      Assist with equipment maintenance, calibration verification, inventory control, and reagent lot tracking.

Cell Culture and Assay Support

·    
  Perform routine mammalian cell culture (primary cells and/or established cell lines), including thawing, passaging, counting, viability assessment, and cryopreservation.
·      Prepare media, buffers, and reagents; maintain aseptic technique and follow biosafety procedures.
·      Support clinical diagnostic assays through sample preparation, plating, labeling, QC checks, and basic data review (per training and authorization).
·      Document deviations, troubleshoot basic workflow issues, and escalate technical concerns to senior staff as appropriate.

Clinical Sample Accessioning and Chain of Custody

·

Job Title: Quality Control Technician

Job Description

The Quality Control Technician performs a wide range of chemical, physical, and instrumental tests on raw materials, in-process products, finished goods, and customer samples to ensure consistent product quality and adherence to specifications. This role follows established analytical procedures, validates methods, manages laboratory data in electronic systems, and collaborates closely with Quality, Production, and R&D teams to support reliable manufacturing processes and continuous improvement.

Responsibilities

Perform chemical, physical, and instrumental testing on raw materials, in-process, finished, and customer product samples, including volumetric and gravimetric analyses, pH measurement, FTIR, SPG, RI, and other instrumental techniques.
Conduct functional testing such as IACS and thermal conductivity as needed to verify product performance.
Follow written analytical procedures and standard operating procedures to ensure consistency and compliance in all testing activities.
Validate established analytical methods and assist in troubleshooting testing procedures to maintain accurate and reliable results.
Collect, enter, review, and validate laboratory data in WinLIMS or similar data management systems, perform necessary calculations, and prepare results for review and approval.
Communicate sample status, test progress, and final results clearly and promptly to Quality, Production, and R&D teams.
Maintain accurate and complete laboratory documentation, including SOPs, test methods, protocols, deviations, batch records, and certificates of analysis (COAs).

jobs.description:
Description

Join Elica’s mission and become a part of a team where every day is an opportunity to make a positive impact in your community!

At Elica Health Centers, we share a common goal: provide the best possible patient care to our growing community! Our passion extends throughout Elica, from the exceptional healthcare services we provide to our underserved patients at our Community Health Clinics and state-of-the-art mobile medicine program, Health on Wheels, to our Resource Center where we empower patients and members of the community to connect with resources to help them build healthy and full lives.

We are growing our Enhanced Care Management (ECM) program at Elica! ECM is a key part of CalAIM’s new statewide Medi-Cal benefit available to select “Populations of Focus" with complex needs and who are facing difficult life and health circumstances. This program is focused on breaking down the traditional walls of health care – extending beyond hospitals and health care settings into communities. ECM will address clinical and non-clinical needs of the highest-need enrollees through intensive coordination of health and health-related services and will meet beneficiaries wherever they are – on the street, in a shelter, in their doctor's office, or at home.

What You'll Do

Care Coordinators assist patients to receive timely and effective care from Elica’s internal providers as well as referrals to community resources outside of Elica. The ultimate goal is well-coordinated care and optimal clinical outcomes. Care Coordinators work with patients individually and within a team environment to achieve these goals and because of their

education & skills, are best able to educate patients as to the health benefits of coordinated care.

Benefits

Retirement Savings Made Easy: Enjoy a 403(b) retirement plan with up to 4% employer matching and 100% immediate vesting—start building your future from day one!
Comprehensive Healthcare Options: Choose from two Anthem Blue Cross PPO plans for medical, plus dental and vision coverage for you and your family.
Employer-Funded HRA: Our Health Reimbursement Arrangement helps cover out-of-pocket medical costs, giving you peace of mind.
Flexible Spending Accounts: Take advantage of two FSA options: Health Care FSA and Dependent Care FSA, tailored to suit your needs.
Security for the Unexpected: We provide company-paid basic Life and AD&D Insurance, with options to enhance coverage.
Enhanced Protection: Explore additional benefits like Hospital Indemnity, Critical Illness, and Accident Insurance, plus ID Theft Protection and Pet Insurance.
Time to Recharge: Enjoy accrued paid time off, paid holidays, and Employee Assistance Plan (EAP) access, which includes counseling, financial, and legal services, along with a vast library of online resources.
Invest in Yourself: Benefit from our Tuition Reimbursement Program for ongoing education and growth, plus CME/CEU and license reimbursements for eligible roles.

This is more than just a benefits package—it’s a commitment to your health, well-being, and professional success!

Learn more about Elica’s services and mission at our website or check us out on Facebook.

Requirements

The successful candidate will be willing and able to:

Patient Coordination: Manage and coordinate patient care activities, ensuring effective communication between patients, healthcare providers, and external agencies. Maintain patient caseloads of 60-200; daily caseload of 12-16 cases/patients per day.
Patient Education: Provide patients and their families with education regarding their health conditions, treatment plans, and available resources.
Scheduling and Follow-Up: Assist patients in scheduling appointments, follow-up visits, and referrals to specialists, ensuring continuity of care.
Bilingual Communication: Utilize bilingual skills (Russian Preferred) to effectively communicate with a diverse patient population, ensuring that language barriers do not hinder the delivery of care.
Documentation: Maintain accurate and up-to-date patient records, including care plans, progress notes, and communication logs at EPIC.
Resource Coordination: Connect patients with community resources, social services, and support programs to address social determinants of health.
Care Plan Development: Collaborate with healthcare providers to develop and implement individualized care plans tailored to each patient's needs.
Team Collaboration: Work closely with other members of the healthcare team to ensure a multidisciplinary approach to patient care.
Quality Improvement: Participate in quality improvement initiatives aimed at enhancing patient care and service delivery.
Compliance and Confidentiality: Adhere to all organizational policies, procedures, and regulations, including patient confidentiality and HIPAA compliance.
Other tasks related to the work of the social care department.

Work Location & Schedule

This position is 100% onsite and does not offer remote or hybrid work options during the first

year of employment.

Work Location: 5735 Watt Avenue, North Highlands, CA 95660
Schedule: Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. – 4:30 p.m. Participation in community

events on weekends as necessary.

Regular, in-person attendance at the office is an essential function of this role due to the nature

of patient coordination, team collaboration, and community-based work.

The Successful Candidate Must Have

Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Healthcare Administration, Nursing, Social Work, or a related field preferred.
Minimum of 2 years of experience in healthcare, preferably in care coordination or patient navigation in the Sacramento, Yolo, or Placer counties.
EHR Experience: Experience working with EPIC electronic health record (EHR) system is preferred.
Experience working with diverse patient populations, including non-English speaking individuals.
Multilingual Russian and Farsi/Dari are highly preferred.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English.
Proficiency in using EPIC EHR for patient documentation, scheduling, and coordination of care.
Basic computer skills, including familiarity with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Google Spaces).

Essential Skills/Abilities

Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build rapport with patients, families, and healthcare team members.
Ability to work effectively in a multidisciplinary team environment.
Excellent organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities efficiently.
Attention to detail and accuracy in maintaining patient records and documentation.
Understanding of healthcare systems, community resources, and social determinants of health.
Knowledge of patient advocacy and care planning principles.
Ability to assess patient needs, identify potential barriers to care, and develop effective solutions.
Familiarity with healthcare regulations, including HIPAA, and commitment to maintaining patient confidentiality.
Ability to adapt to changes in a fast-paced healthcare environment and support continuous quality improvement initiative

Additional Requirements

Must have a current and valid California driver’s license and the ability to provide proof of personal auto insurance on the vehicle driven during working hours.

Physical Requirements And Work Environment

The work environment is office, clinic and field based administering program education and Care Coordination to Adults, Children and Youth and recent immigrants. Work environment includes office, clinic, field work. Employees are to adhere to field visit policies, including, but not limited to being accompanied by a colleague while working with clients in a not public setting. The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to walk; use hands to finger, handle, or feel. The employee is also required to stand; walk; and reach with hands and arms. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 20 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, and the ability to adjust focus. The employee must also possess hearing and speech to communicate in person and over the phone. The noise level in the work environment can range from quiet to moderately loud; the incumbent must be able to focus in an environment with many distractions.

The employee may be in contact with individuals and families in crisis who may be ill, using substances and/or not attentive to personal health. The employee may experience a number of unpleasant sensory demands associated with the client’s use of alcohol and drugs, and the lack of personal care. The employee may also be exposed to bio-hazardous materials (bodily fluids including blood and urine) and hazardous chemicals. The employee must be ready to respond quickly and effectively to many types of situations, including crisis situations and potentially hostile situations.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

jobs.title: Data Analyst – Analytics & Strategy
jobs.description:
At cabi, we're redefining what it means to build a fashion brand—one rooted in connection, confidence, and purpose. As a women's retail clothing company, we don't just design beautiful apparel; we create opportunities for women to express themselves, build community, and thrive both personally and professionally. Our culture is collaborative, entrepreneurial, and deeply people-first, and every team member plays a role in creating meaningful experiences for our Stylists and clients. If you're energized by creativity, inspired by empowering others, and excited to contribute to a brand that blends style with substance, you'll feel right at home here.

We are looking for a Data Analyst who can own our recurring reporting and also dig into the open-ended questions that come up across the business. About half of the role is keeping our core reporting accurate, reliable, and increasingly automated. The other half is ad hoc analysis and project work, where you'll partner with teams across the company to answer the questions behind their biggest decisions.

This role is a great fit for someone who enjoys both building things that run smoothly and solving new problems. You should be comfortable taking a loosely defined request, figuring out what's really being asked, and turning it into a clear analysis and recommendation. Because our work goes to executives, the board, and external partners, a high attention to detail is essential.

We also use AI tools every day to work faster and smarter, and we're looking for someone who is excited to do the same.

  

**What You'll Do**

Reporting, maintenance, and automation

* + Own and maintain a portfolio of recurring reports and Tableau dashboards used by executives and teams across the company
* + Monitor data refreshes and pipelines, troubleshoot issues quickly, and keep stakeholders informed when something breaks
* + Find manual or repetitive reporting work and automate it, using SQL, scripting, and AI tools to make reporting faster and more reliable
* + Build and maintain data transformation pipelines in our cloud data warehouse (Snowflake) that feed reporting and analysis
* + Write clear documentation for reports, metric definitions, and data logic so the team can support each other's work
* + Validate data and check your work so the numbers we publish can be trusted

Ad hoc analysis and projects

* + Partner with stakeholders across the company to understand the business questions behind their requests
* + Turn vague or loosely defined asks into specific questions, scoped analyses, and clear timelines
* + Help develop data products for teams across the organization that keep them informed and guide their decision making
* + Design and build new Tableau dashboards from the ground up, from gathering requirements and modeling the data to final design
* + Run analyses that apply statistical techniques to uncover trends, patterns, and correlations, explain performance, and identify opportunities, then present findings in plain language with clear recommendations
* + Guide stakeholders through what the data means for their decisions, including where it has limits
* + Use AI tools to speed up analysis, explore new approaches, and prototype solutions, and share what you learn with the team

**What You Bring**

* + 2–4 years of experience in data analytics, business intelligence, or a related role
* + Strong SQL skills and experience working in a cloud data warehouse such as Snowflake
* + Hands-on experience building Tableau dashboards from scratch, including data modeling, calculations, and thoughtful visual design
* + Experience building or maintaining data transformation pipelines
* + Regular, practical use of AI tools in your work, and genuine curiosity about how AI can change the way analytics gets done
* + Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including explaining technical findings to non-technical audiences
* + Ability to take an ambiguous request, ask the right questions, and turn it into a focused analysis
* + High attention to detail: you catch errors before anyone else does, sanity-check numbers against what you know about the business, and hold yourself to a standard of accuracy fit for executive and board reporting
* + Comfort managing several priorities at once and keeping stakeholders updated on progress
* + Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field such as analytics, statistics, economics, computer science, or business, or equivalent experience
* + A collaborative mindset and eagerness to work across teams in a fast-moving environment
* + A strong team player who supports colleagues and takes ownership and accountability for the team's work

**Nice to Have**

* + Experience with dbt or a similar transformation tool
* + Python for data processing, automation, or analysis
* + Experience in retail, fashion, direct sales, or another consumer business
* + Familiarity with performance marketing and acquisition platforms such as Google Analytics, Meta, Instagram, and TikTok
* + Familiarity with Tableau Server or Tableau Cloud administration

jobs.title: Scientist III, Bioinformatics (Companion Diagnostics)
jobs.description:
**Work Schedule**

Standard (Mon-Fri)

**Environmental Conditions**

Office

**Job Description**

**Discover Impactful Work**

At Thermo Fisher Scientific, our mission is to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner, and safer. Our CDx Bioinformatics team contributes to that mission by supporting the development of next-generation sequencing companion diagnostics that help guide cancer treatment.

As a Scientist III, Bioinformatics, you will apply your knowledge of biology, oncology, and genomic data analysis to active diagnostic development programs. Your work will include preparing study datasets, investigating sequencing results, and developing tools that improve the quality and efficiency of scientific analysis.

You will join a collaborative team and work with colleagues in Research and Development, Program Management, Clinical Affairs, Biostatistics, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, and Software Development. This role offers opportunities to contribute across multiple programs, deepen your expertise in regulated diagnostic development, and apply new computational approaches, including AI-assisted tools, with sound scientific judgment.

**What You Will Do**

* Prepare, curate, and review study datasets, including variant and quality-control line listings, sample metadata, and data transfer packages. Reconcile source data and resolve missing, inconsistent, or unexpected results before delivery.
* Analyze DNA and RNA sequencing results in the context of assay design, oncology biomarkers, and study requirements. Assess variant coverage, reporting eligibility, and differences between assays or analysis configurations.
* Investigate discordant results, unexpected variant calls, no-calls, and quality-control findings. Review sequencing evidence and analysis settings, document the findings, and explain what the evidence does and does not support.
* Prepare program-specific assay definition inputs, including hotspot and variant content files, and perform reanalyses using defined software and configuration versions.
* Provide analyses and technical documentation for study reports, regulatory questions, and partner requests. Maintain traceability to source data, methods, and analysis versions.
* Develop and improve scripts and tools for recurring tasks such as dataset curation, variant comparison, quality checks, and reporting. Test changes, participate in code review, and document methods so others can use and maintain them.
* Use approved AI-assisted tools where useful for coding, troubleshooting, data exploration, and documentation. Independently verify generated code and content before use, with appropriate protection of confidential data.
* Manage assigned deliverables across multiple programs, clarify requirements with collaborators, and communicate findings, dependencies, and delivery risks.

**Qualifications**

**Education and Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree with at least five years of relevant experience, or an advanced degree with at least three years of relevant experience, in bioinformatics, computational biology, molecular biology, or a related field.
* Hands-on experience analyzing NGS data in oncology, molecular diagnostics, or a closely related setting.
* Experience preparing and reviewing scientific datasets for use by other teams or external collaborators.

**Scientific and Technical Skills**

* Strong understanding of molecular biology, cancer genomics, and the relationship between genomic alterations and diagnostic assay design.
* Working knowledge of NGS data processing, variant calling, sequencing quality metrics, and sources of technical error. Experience with Linux/Unix, Git, and common sequencing data formats such as BAM and VCF.
* Experience interpreting relevant variant classes, such as SNVs, indels, copy-number alterations, gene fusions, and splice variants.
* Proficiency in Python or another suitable analysis language, including the ability to write, troubleshoot, and review code independently.
* Ability to reconcile data from multiple sources and build reproducible analyses with documented assumptions and quality checks.
* Practical familiarity with AI-assisted tools and their limitations, including the ability to identify and correct unsupported or incorrect outputs.
* Ability to explain technical findings clearly, distinguish evidence from assumptions, and recognize when further analysis or specialist input is needed.

**Preferred Experience**

* Companion diagnostic development or analytical and clinical validation studies.
* Targeted oncology sequencing of FFPE tissue or plasma specimens.
* Work in a regulated or quality-controlled environment, including documented analysis methods, version control, and review requirements.
* Preparation of partner data transfers, study-report datasets, or analyses supporting regulatory submissions.

**Compensation and Benefits**

The salary range estimated for this position based in Texas is $89,800.00–$122,000.00.

This position may also be eligible to receive a variable annual bonus based on company, team, and/or individual performance results in accordance with company policy. We offer a comprehensive Total Rewards package that our U.S. colleagues and their families can count on, which includes:

* A choice of national medical and dental plans, and a national vision plan, including health incentive programs
* Employee assistance and family support programs, including commuter benefits and tuition reimbursement
* At least 120 hours paid time off (PTO), 10 paid holidays annually, paid parental leave (3 weeks for bonding and 8 weeks for caregiver leave), accident and life insurance, and short- and long-term disability in accordance with company policy

jobs.title: Test Lab Technician
jobs.description:
**Summary:** Set up static, motion, vibration, flow, and environmental tests. Make instrumentation for electrical and mechanical measurements of test conditions. Make neat and complete records of test results. Note and evaluate any unusual events occurring during progress of test for additional reporting.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

Under general supervision, must be able to perform a variety of job duties including, but not limited to:

* Makes any mechanical set-up and jigs for same with a minimum amount of supervision.
* Assists supervisors and engineers to achieve proper test methods and set-up.
* Sets up and performs vibration test, shock tests, flow tests (both liquid and gaseous), helium leak detection, cycle testing (hydraulic and pneumatic), and environmental testing.
* Works with all power equipment such as lathe, band saws, grinders, drill presses, shock testers, cycling equipment, leak detector, vibrators and other necessary power equipment to conduct such tests.
* Works with recording instruments.
* Works with micrometers, venire calipers, and other measuring instruments.
* Reads schematic drawings and Engineering blueprints.
* Uses shop mathematics and trigonometry.
* Performs all functions with safety and neatness.
* Make legible substantiating data on all tests performed.
* Caps, plug and clamp parts for pressure tests. Makes and maintain test rigs for motion and fatigue cycling. Tends furnaces and other heating apparatus for temperature testing.
* Runs tensile test. Finds yield point and elongation of metals.
* Performs rework, repair and other associated operations in connection with the work described.
* Understands helium leak detector, can service, change filaments and maintain machine.
* Repairs electrical equipment used for measurement and testing.
* Mounts, polishes, etches, and photographs samples for microscopic examination.
* Communicates progress and problems associated with operation sin the development of an assigned project to their supervisor.
* Be qualified to weld any materials in Groups I, II, III, IV & VI for test setups of high-pressure, high temperature applications.
* Follow all Senior policies and procedures.
* Other duties with the work as assigned.

.

Pay: $40.00 - $45.00 per hour

Expected hours: No less than 40.0 per week

Work Location: In person

jobs.title: Quality Control Technician
jobs.description:
**Position Summary:**  
The Quality Control (QC) Technician is responsible for ensuring Calbee’s food products meet established food safety and quality standards through routine testing, inspection, and documentation. Working under the direction of the Quality Supervisor and Quality Management, this role monitors production processes, evaluates in-process and finished products, and identifies and communicates quality concerns.
  
  
The QC Technician must demonstrate attention to detail, integrity, and sound judgment while working collaboratively with Production and other departments to maintain a safe, consistent, and high-quality product.
  
  
**Responsibilities:**  

* Perform physical inspections, analytical testing, and sensory evaluations of in-process and finished products to verify compliance with Calbee’s food safety and quality standards.
* Conduct quality control checks, including seal integrity, date code verification, metal detection monitoring, weight checks, and label accuracy.
* Maintain an active presence on the production floor to monitor product quality and compliance with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs), housekeeping standards, and company procedures.
* Identify, document, and promptly communicate food safety concerns, quality issues, and nonconforming products.
* Place affected products on hold in accordance with established procedures and support the review and assessment of quality and food safety concerns.
* Provide feedback and support corrective actions when nonconformance issues are identified.
* Conduct preoperational inspections of equipment and processing areas at the start of shifts and during line changeovers.
* Perform sanitation verification and environmental testing, including ATP and allergen testing.
* Collect, organize, and maintain retain samples for shelf-life evaluation.
* Calibrate and maintain laboratory equipment according to established schedules and accurately document calibration activities.
* Complete inspection records, test results, and other required documentation accurately, truthfully, and in real time.
* Comply with applicable SQF requirements, food safety policies, quality standards, GMPs, and company procedures.
* Support smooth shift transitions through clear verbal and written handoffs.
* Assist in training new QC Technicians on testing procedures, production-line inspections, and documentation requirements.
* Comply with all applicable SQF requirements, food safety policies, quality standards, GMPs, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) relevant to the position.
* Perform additional duties as assigned by Quality Management.

**Qualifications:**  

* Minimum of one year of quality control, quality assurance, or food safety experience in a food manufacturing environment required; two or more years preferred.
* High school diploma or equivalent required.
* Hands-on experience performing product inspections, quality testing, and documentation in a production environment.
* Working knowledge of GMPs, Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP), and food safety and quality systems.
* Familiarity with Safe Quality Food (SQF) requirements preferred.
* Experience with ATP and allergen testing, product sampling, and laboratory equipment calibration preferred.
* Strong attention to detail, analytical skills, and sound judgment when evaluating results and identifying concerns.
* Ability to read, understand, and follow documented protocols and SOPs.
* Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to communicate findings and provide clear shift handoffs.
* Self-motivated and able to work independently with minimal supervision while contributing to a team.
* Commitment to integrity, professionalism, accurate documentation, and reliable attendance.
* Ability to work flexible hours, including occasional weekends, overtime, and holidays based on production needs.
* Ability to lift and carry up to 25 pounds and perform activities such as reaching, stooping, and climbing stairs.

#LI-DNI
  
  
Calbee North America is an equal opportunity employer dedicated to a policy of non-discrimination in employment on the basis of race, color, age, sex, religion, national origin, disability, veteran status, citizenship, ancestry, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital or familial status or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Part-time Lab Technician
jobs.description:
**About Jeevan**

Jeevan is a climate technology company developing novel carbon capture systems. Our work is hands-on, experimental, and fast-moving, with a strong emphasis on benchtop testing, prototyping, and data integrity. This role supports our core R&D efforts in our Alhambra facility.

**Role Overview**

This is a hands-on role combining bench-scale laboratory work with physical prototype assembly and test rig setup. The ideal candidate is comfortable both running controlled experiments and working with tools to build, modify, and troubleshoot small-scale systems. This role is well-suited to someone who enjoys building things as much as testing them.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Support Jeevan’s benchtop laboratory experiments under the direction of the Lab Director.
* Prepare common lab solutions and reagents based on target specifications (e.g., calculate and prepare solutions to a desired concentration, pH, and volume).
* Conduct routine bench-scale lab experiments following written instructions (e.g., resin/column tests, batch mixing, timed procedures), and proactively communicate questions or issues.
* Operate basic lab equipment as trained, including balances, pH meters, conductivity meters, stir plates, and peristaltic pumps; verify equipment is functioning properly prior to use.
* Collect, label, and store samples properly; perform basic measurements (pH, conductivity, mass, volume) and record results in a consistent format.
* Maintain clear, organized experimental notes (including dates, procedures, calculations, deviations, and observations) and upload data and photos to shared folders.
* Monitor experiments during runs (e.g., flow rate, leaks, temperature, system stability) and immediately document abnormalities or failures.
* Clean and organize work areas, glassware, and lab tools; manage routine lab waste disposal in accordance with safety guidelines.
* Contribute to experimental design and assist with equipment assembly and test setup.
* Maintain material and equipment inventory, including tracking supply needs and assisting with ordering or local pickup when required.
* Assemble and modify benchtop and pilot-scale test rigs, including tubing runs, fittings, pumps, filters, housings, and support frames.
* Use basic hand tools (wrenches, drills, saws, tubing cutters, etc.) to fabricate and adjust prototype components.
* Troubleshoot mechanical and fluid system issues (e.g., leaks, loose fittings, flow restrictions) and implement practical fixes.
* Assist in building and maintaining scale models and early-stage prototype systems.
* Support physical setup and teardown of experiments, including moving equipment and reconfiguring systems between test runs.

**Qualifications**

* Availability for 15 - 25 hours per week during standard working hours (8:00am–5:00pm ET).
* Ability to reliably commute to and from our lab at 1135 Westminster Ave, Unit K, Alhambra, CA.
* Prior laboratory experience (academic, research, or industry) preferred.
* Comfort working with basic lab equipment and following written experimental procedures.
* Strong attention to detail and willingness to document work clearly and consistently.
* Ability to work independently while communicating issues promptly and clearly.
* Prior experience with hands-on mechanical work, fabrication, or prototyping is strongly preferred.

**Work Authorization**

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States for the hours listed.

**Physical Requirements**

* Ability to stand for extended periods and perform hands-on lab work.
* Ability to lift and move light lab equipment and materials (generally under 25 lbs).
* Ability to safely handle lab materials while following safety protocols.

**How to Apply**

Please apply with:

* A brief introduction
* Your resume
* Your availability (days/times during the week)

Pay: $25.00 - $30.00 per hour

Expected hours: 15.0 – 25.0 per week

Work Location: In person

Sample Preparation

Prioritizes and performs a wide variety of clinical laboratory tests on various biological specimens. Reviews, evaluates, documents and reports results. Preserves confidentiality of patients and follows lab safety and maintenance protocols. Trains and supervises trainees, laboratory assistants and clerks as needed.

jobs.title: Senior Research Associate, Preclinical Pharmacology
jobs.description:
**Senior Research Associate, Preclinical Pharmacology**

*Run in vivo studies that move Nurix's degrader programs toward the clinic. You'll execute mouse efficacy, PK/PD, and mechanism-of-action studies in oncology and inflammation models and generate the Western blot and flow cytometry data that show how our molecules work.*

**Position Description**

**The Opportunity**

* Join the Research – Preclinical Pharmacology team as a full-time, onsite, hands-on member, reporting to a Scientist / Principal Scientist, Preclinical Pharmacology
* Perform mouse handling and in-life procedures, including dosing by oral (PO), intraperitoneal (IP), subcutaneous (SC), and intravenous (IV) routes, tumor cell implantation, tumor and body-weight measurements, and in-life and terminal blood collection
* Execute PK/PD, tolerability, and efficacy studies in oncology xenograft/syngeneic models and in murine models of inflammation, under the direction of study leads
* Prepare and formulate test articles and vehicles for dosing; monitor animal health, document observations, and escalate adverse events promptly
* Perform necropsy and collect, process, and bank tissues and blood for downstream biomarker and pharmacodynamic analyses
* Prepare tissue and cell lysates and perform Western blotting (including quantitative and automated capillary formats) to measure target degradation and pathway modulation
* Develop, run, and analyze multi-color flow cytometry panels for immune and tumor-cell phenotyping from blood, spleen, tumor, and other tissues
* Maintain and expand cell lines using sterile cell culture technique; support cell-based assays and the generation of cells for in vivo implantation
* Record experiments accurately and in a timely manner in the electronic lab notebook; analyze, graph, and summarize data and present results at team meetings
* Collaborate with Biology, Chemistry, DMPK, and Translational teams to design studies and troubleshoot models and assays
* Adhere to IACUC protocols, animal welfare regulations, and laboratory safety requirements, and maintain required training and certifications
* Contribute to the optimization and qualification of new models and assays and to the training of junior team members
* Maintain laboratory equipment and supplies and support vivarium coordination, including occasional weekend or off-shift study coverage; other essential duties as assigned; minimal travel (<5%)

**What You'll Bring**

* BS/MS in Biology, Pharmacology, Immunology, Cancer Biology, or a related field, with a BS or equivalent plus 8 or more years of relevant experience, or an MS plus 4 or more years of relevant experience
* Industry (biotech or pharma) experience conducting in vivo pharmacology studies in mice
* Proficiency in mouse handling and dosing by PO, IP, SC, and IV routes, as well as blood collection and tissue harvest
* Hands-on experience with oncology models (e.g., xenograft, syngeneic) and with murine models of inflammation or immunology
* Demonstrated proficiency in Western blotting and flow cytometry, including sample preparation, staining, and data analysis
* Proficiency in sterile mammalian cell culture technique
* Working knowledge of IACUC regulations and humane animal care practices
* Strong organizational and documentation skills, with attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple studies simultaneously
* Collaborative, adaptable, and comfortable in a fast-paced, team-oriented research environment
* Ability to work in an animal facility and tolerate exposure to laboratory animals, and to work occasional weekends or off-shift hours as studies require
* Bonus: experience with targeted protein degradation (molecular glues, PROTACs) or other small-molecule oncology or immunology programs
* Bonus: experience with multi-spectral flow cytometry, automated Western (e.g., Jess/Wes), ELISA, or MSD cytokine/biomarker assays
* Bonus: experience with orthotopic, disseminated, PDX, or humanized mouse models, or with in vivo imaging
* Bonus: experience with inflammation models such as collagen-induced arthritis, colitis, or cytokine-challenge models
* Bonus: familiarity with PK/PD relationships, compound formulation, and dose-response study design
* Bonus: proficiency with GraphPad Prism and electronic lab notebook systems

**Salary Range:** $131,400 - $139,900

*The posted range applies to roles based in the San Francisco Bay Area and reflects local market conditions. Where an offer lands within that range depends on the candidate's relevant experience, technical expertise, and how their background aligns with the role's requirements.*

**Location:** Onsite – Brisbane, CA

  

**Fit with Nurix Culture and Values**

* Strong team orientation; highly collaborative
* Solutions and results-oriented focus
* Hands-on approach; resourceful and open to diverse points of view

**About Nurix Therapeutics**

*Nurix Therapeutics is a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of targeted protein degradation medicines, the next frontier in innovative drug design aimed at improving treatment options for patients with cancer and inflammatory diseases. Powered by a fully AI-integrated discovery engine capable of tackling any protein class, and coupled with unparalleled ligase expertise, Nurix's dedicated team has built a formidable advantage in translating the science of targeted protein degradation into clinical advancements. Nurix aims to establish degrader-based treatments at the forefront of patient care, writing medicine's next chapter with a new script to outmatch disease.*

About The Role

What if your native German fluency could help teach AI how to handle a real phone call to a doctor's office? We're looking for native German speakers based in the New York area to hold natural spoken conversations with an AI healthcare receptionist, then evaluate how well it listens, responds, and takes action.

New York's large German-speaking community — from recent expats to heritage speakers — makes it an ideal place to find people with the authentic, natural German speech this project demands. You'll role-play as a patient using fictional personas we provide, record short conversations, and grade the AI's performance.

This is a fully remote, flexible contract role for people with clear German speech, strong attention to detail, and an ear for what sounds natural and fluent.

Organization: Alignerr
Type: Contract (task-based)
Location: Remote
Commitment: Flexible, work at your own pace

What You'll Do

Hold 4 to 5 minute spoken conversations in German with an AI front desk assistant, playing a fictional patient
Say natural trigger phrases to test whether the AI makes the correct function calls — for example, checking a patient record, booking an appointment, or verifying insurance
Review transcripts and classify how accurately the AI understood you and responded
Flag issues such as mispronunciations, cutoffs, interruptions, delays, and incorrect function calls, including timestamps
Test how the AI handles background noise, short replies such as "ja," "nein," or "okay," long numbers, emotional moments, and sensitive or unsafe requests
Follow detailed labeling guidelines consistently and submit high-quality work

Who You Are

Native or near-native German speaker with a clear, natural speaking voice

Able to follow multi-step instructions and apply them consistently

Comfortable using web-based tools

Nice to Have

Experience in voice AI evaluation, data annotation, or QA testing
Background in healthcare administration, customer service, or call centre work
Familiarity with spoken German variants from Germany, Austria, and Switzerland
Linguistics or language-focused academic background
Familiarity with medical terminology in German

Why Join Us

Work on cutting-edge AI projects alongside leading research labs
Fully remote and flexible — work when and where it suits you
Task-based work with real autonomy
Directly help make voice AI more accurate, natural, and safe in healthcare settings
Potential for ongoing work as new projects launch

jobs.description:
Company Overview

Sarmal, Inc. is a San Diego–based biotechnology company developing next-generation genomics and molecular detection platforms. Our work integrates molecular biology, chemistry, and advanced systems engineering to enable faster, more precise, and more accessible genomic insights.

We are a highly collaborative, R&D-driven team operating in a fast-paced, early-stage environment. Our scientists and engineers work across disciplines to solve complex technical challenges and translate innovation into scalable, real-world applications.

At Sarmal, we value scientific rigor, curiosity, and a builder mindset. We are looking for individuals who are energized by ambiguity, motivated by impact, and excited to help bring breakthrough technologies from concept to reality.

About The Job

Sarmal is seeking a Research Technician to support routine batch execution and core analytical measurements for a biosensor device platform's surface chemistry processes. This is a hands-on, execution-focused role — running defined procedures under direct RA/scientist supervision, maintaining careful documentation, and building toward greater independence over time. Suited to candidates with foundational lab experience (academic, co-op, or early industry); strong execution and reliability may open the door to broader involvement in experimental support work as the program progresses. Open to early-career candidates with relevant hands-on lab training; not intended for a fully independent, self-directed hire.

Key Responsibilities

Execute surface functionalization batch runs (SAM, silane, hydrogel, brush polymer chemistries) per written SOPs/batch records, under direct RA/scientist supervision.
Operate the team's core surface characterization methods — fluorescence-based uniformity assays and contact angle — for routine batch checks, with EIS/CV support as trained.
Record characterization results (thickness, density, uniformity, charge) accurately and completely for RA/scientist review.
Assist with surface deposition/patterning process runs (spin-coating, dip-coating, spray-coating, plasma treatment/activation; exposure to PE-CVD/CVD or photolithographic patterning a plus).
Prepare samples and run defined test conditions for DOE test plans as directed by RA/scientist staff.
Log data accurately and promptly in lab notebooks/ELN; flag deviations from expected process parameters to RA/scientist staff.
Maintain organized inventory of chemistry consumables and reagents used in daily runs.
Maintain cleanroom/lab space per site protocols.
Work collaboratively with in-house RAs and scientists; follow established procedures precisely and escalate issues rather than resolving independently.

Qualifications

Hands-on lab experience (academic or industry) with interfacial materials or related wet-chemistry techniques; comfort executing established analytical methods (e.g., contact angle, fluorescence-based assays) with training.
Ability to follow detailed written procedures (SOPs, batch records) precisely and consistently.
Strong attention to detail and reliability; comfortable following defined test procedures exactly as written in a fast-paced environment.
Comfort with structured documentation (batch records, ELN, GDP-style recordkeeping).

Education

B.S. in Chemistry, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, Biology, or related field (or equivalent hands-on lab training) + 0–2 years of relevant lab experience — academic, or industry — with surface chemistry, thin-film processes, or related wet-chemistry techniques

Benefits & Perks

Sarmal offers a competitive and comprehensive benefits package, including:

Medical, dental, and vision coverage
Company-paid life insurance
401(k) retirement plan
Generous paid time off
Access to additional voluntary benefits, employee perks, and discount programs

ABOUT US:
The VERBIO Nevada Biorefinery
, located in Nevada, Iowa (USA), is the first industrial scale renewable natural gas (RNG) facility in North America using agricultural residues as its feedstock. The plant is 100% owned by VERBIO North America Holdings Corporation. RNG production from corn stover began in December 2021 with the completion of Phase I, at a capacity of 7 million ethanol gallons equivalent (EGE) per year. Upon completion of Phase II in the 4th quarter of 2022, the site will begin operating as a biorefinery, producing 60 million gallons of corn-based ethanol and an additional 19 million (EGE) of RNG from stillage. The integration of RNG and ethanol production, unique to VERBIO, incorporates advanced operational technology currently practiced at the company’s facilities in Germany. The process also yields humus, a soil amendment, and organic fertilizers. VERBIO Vereinigte BioEnergie AG (VERBIO AG)
, with headquarters in Leipzig, Germany, is a leading independent manufacturer of biofuels and bioenergy in Germany and Europe. The company began producing biofuel in 2001 and today has approximately 900 employees at its locations in Germany, Poland, Hungary, India, USA and Canada producing biodiesel, bioethanol and biomethane (renewable natural gas), as well as feed, bio-fertilizers and other high-value by-products for the nutrition, pharmaceutical and cosmetics industries, all on an industrial scale. VERBIO concentrates on the use of internally developed innovative and efficient energy-saving production processes. With its innovative processes and highly efficient production plants, VERBIO is a technology leader in the biofuels market. Energy production from renewable resources is the key component of the world’s future energy mix. Renewable raw materials have the potential to permanently replace fossil fuels and simultaneously solve the problem of surplus agricultural production in North America and elsewhere. It is VERBIO’s goal to be a leader in 21st century alternative green energy solutions. As we consolidate and expand our position as one of the world’s leading biofuels producers, we will leverage our technologies and the value of agriculture to create renewable and sustainable solutions globally, while pursing solid growth and responsible relationships with our stakeholders: farmers, customers, employees, shareholders, partners, researchers, consumers, governmental entities, and interest groups. Our Mission
VERBIO North America is committed to the principle of sustainability and treats natural resources in a socially responsible and ethical manner. Using the latest technologies, developed in-house, we are creating sustainable alternatives for a world whose desire is to move away from fossil fuels. Our business model endeavors to ignite change and create platforms where the path to green energy is contagious. With our fuels cutting greenhouse gas emissions by up to 90% compared to fossil fuels, we are showing the way forward in climate protection. And with a vision for a greener future, we are building strong competence centers and competitive production facilities in different parts of the world, while our employees partner alongside farmers to safeguard the environment for current and future generations. Our Approach

Be creative, innovative, ethical, and fast in execution.
Partner with agriculture to safeguard land and natural resources for future generations.

Maintain accurate and detailed electronic laboratory notebooks and manage inventory of synthesized compounds and related materials.
Operate, maintain, and troubleshoot laboratory equipment and analytical instrumentation.
Analyze and interpret experimental data and present findings at project and departmental meetings.

Qualifications

Strong understanding of modern organic chemistry techniques in literature and in laboratory. 
Hands-on experience organic chemistry synthesis techniques including air- and moisture-sensitive reactions using Schlenk techniques and inert atmosphere conditions.
Proficiency in operating analytical instrumentation such as HPLC and LC-MS with the ability to interpret results from data acquisition. 
Strong analytical chemistry skills using LC-MS, NMR, IR, UV/Vis, TLC, and related techniques.
Experience in chemoenzymatic reactions is a plus.
Strong documentation and scientific communication skills.
Strong sense of teamwork, flexibility, and enthusiasm for advancing new technologies.

jobs.description:
JOB TITLE: Engineering Specialist

LOCATION: San Francisco or Sacramento

JOB OPENING #: 6780

OVERVIEW 

The Judicial Council of California is accepting applications for the position of Engineering Specialist (Energy & Sustainability) with the Facilities Services office.

The Engineering Specialist will be responsible for analyzing and validating utility data, including electricity, natural gas, water, waste, and fuels, for courthouses in the assigned regions in Central and Southern California. The role supports sustainability-focused decision-making by identifying usage trends, verifying billing accuracy, and flagging inefficiencies. A significant focus is on maintaining high-quality data in platforms such as ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager and the Energy Management Information System (EMIS) to support energy reduction, water conservation, and decarbonization goals.

The Engineering Specialist supports the monthly and annual reporting of energy and water use, costs, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, as well as regulatory compliance reporting, including GHG inventory data compilation and support for Assembly Bill (AB) 802 benchmarking. Trend analysis to identify peak demand, abnormal water use, and inefficiencies is a key aspect of this work.

This position also involves conducting or supporting energy and water audits, life cycle cost analysis, and technical reviews of mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems in support of energy efficiency, water efficiency, and waste reduction upgrades and capital project planning. The Engineering Specialist helps identify and track utility incentives and rebates, recommends energy- and water-efficient equipment, and contributes to the development of energy, water conservation, and waste reduction policy. The position serves as the technical water and waste resource for the Sustainability Unit and provides related educational training for the field staff and court staff.

The Judicial Council 

The Judicial Council of California is the policy setting body for the state court system and has constitutionally conferred statewide rule-making authority. This authority includes developing, advocating for, and allocating the judicial branch budget. A majority of Council members are California state justices and judges; however, the Council also includes lawyers, legislators, and court administrators.

By enhancing its role as a leadership, knowledge, and service resource for the judicial branch, the Judicial Council’s staff organization seeks to continue to evolve as one of California’s most dynamic public service entities, focused on improving access to justice for all Californians by innovating and responding to the changing needs of the courts and the public. As a government body charged with improving the statewide administration of justice, the Judicial Council has multiple offices with diverse responsibilities relating to court policy and operations. As employees of the council, every member of staff should view and approach their work as one Judicial Council with a public service mission that is greater than the sum of its parts.

The Judicial Council strives for work-life balance, including substantial vacation and holiday time. In addition, we offer an excellent benefits package, including pension, medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible spending, up to $130 per month reimbursement for qualifying commuting costs, student loan forgiveness as part of Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), and retirement savings plans. In San Francisco, the office is only a 7-minute walk from the Civic Center BART station. In Sacramento, the office is minutes from downtown, just north of Discovery Park.

The Judicial Council offers hybrid work arrangements for many positions. The successful candidate will be expected to work in person at the Judicial Council’s San Francisco or Sacramento office at least two days per week, based on their office leader’s direction, and reside in the areas surrounding these locations. To be eligible for Judicial Council employment and participation in the Judicial Council’s Hybrid Work Program, a prospective or current employee’s primary residence/remote work location must be in the State of California and within a 150-mile driving radius of their assigned reporting location.

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Review and validate utility bills for electricity, natural gas, water, waste, and fuels for courthouses in the assigned regions, including daily batch reviews, late bill monitoring, and accurate entry of paper and electronic invoices in the EMIS.
• Monitor utility data quality across the portfolio in the EMIS and ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager, identify discrepancies, and coordinate corrections with utility vendors, Branch Accounting, Procurement, and other internal stakeholders.
• Serve as the utility vendor liaison for the assigned regions, resolving billing discrepancies, service concerns, payment issues, and account setup for new and transferred facilities.

jobs.title: AI Trainer - PHYSICS
jobs.description:
About The Role

Our client is looking for experienced scientists and engineers to evaluate how frontier AI models handle real technical work: analyzing test, measurement or process data, sizing and verifying a design, designing an experiment and reading it out, interpreting a simulation, writing the technical report. You bring the judgment you have built catching the unit error in a test file, the multiple comparisons trap in a process improvement study, and the assumption that does not hold at the boundary. We bring the model output that judgment is needed to grade.

In this role, you will design challenging, realistic tasks drawn from your own practice, such as a calculation package with stated assumptions and checks, a test plan and data analysis, a failure or deviation investigation, a design trade study, an experimental protocol with acceptance criteria, a circuit or system design review, or a technical report, run them through frontier AI agents, and evaluate what comes back against a professional standard.

Across our STEM and Data Science programs, tasks are grounded in real day-to-day workflows and checked against frontier models so only genuinely hard tasks make it through. Some projects are authored and verified in code, so coding / scientific computing is a strong plus and is required on those projects.

You will work with realistic professional files, the kind a practitioner in your field actually handles, which you assemble yourself. Some tasks are compact, built around a handful of files; others are larger scenarios that take several days to build. In every case the goal is the same: a task a competent professional in your field would complete correctly and a frontier model currently gets wrong.

This is not a traditional science or engineering role. You will be helping build better AI by putting your knowledge to work in a structured, flexible, fully remote environment. The work is long-form and self-directed, and clear written reasoning matters as much as technical depth.

Responsibilities

Design challenging, realistic technical tasks drawn from your own day-to-day work: the scenario, a prompt phrased the way you would brief a trusted colleague, and the supporting files an engineer or scientist would need (test data, drawings or schematics, specifications, simulation outputs, lab records, reports), which you author yourself.
Run those tasks through frontier AI models and evaluate the deliverable they produce (the calculation, analysis, design review or report) against the standard you would hold a colleague to.
Compare two model outputs on identical prompts and files, decide which performed better, and document where each fell short.
Write detailed grading rubrics that specify what a correct deliverable must contain (the right assumptions stated, the right method, the right magnitudes and units, the right failure modes considered), and explain in writing why a response passes or fails each one.
Flag concrete failures with evidence: unit and scaling errors, misread data, unsupported conclusions, fabricated or ignored source files, missed safety or boundary conditions, and off-brief interpretation of the ask.
Contribute across your discipline and adjacent ones, and review and refine tasks built by other experts.

Qualifications

2+ years of applied experience preferred in one of the core sciences (mathematics, physics, chemistry, or biology) or in an engineering discipline (electrical and electronics, civil and structural, materials, chemical and process, environmental and earth sciences, or similar) or in data science.
In progress Bachelor’s degree or higher. We prefer 2+ years of experience outside undergraduate study.
Coding / scientific computing is a strong plus and is required on some projects: comfortable writing and verifying work in code (Python or similar) and working at the command line.
Hands-on with real data and the tools of your field: instrument and test data, measurement files, simulation outputs, schematics or drawings, and the analysis tools that go with them (MATLAB, Python or R; SPICE and PCB tools; FEA or CFD; GIS; chromatography or spectroscopy software).
Comfort with statistical and experimental reasoning: experiment design, measurement error and uncertainty, and the common statistical traps. The assessment leans on this.
Working understanding of adjacent sub-disciplines, enough to assess work outside your own specialty and point out what was done correctly or incorrectly.
Hands-on practitioner: you currently do (or recently did) the work yourself at an individual-contributor level, not solely in a managerial capacity.
Full professional or native-level written and spoken English; you can articulate why a result is wrong, not only that it is.
General familiarity with AI and LLM tools: you can tell a well-reasoned answer from a plausible-sounding but incorrect one.
Baseline tech literacy: comfortable with cloud file tools (e.g., Google Workspace), managing browser profiles, downloading and installing desktop apps (e.g., Claude), and everyday file handling (e.g., converting between Excel and Google Sheets, zipping files for sharing).
Advanced degree or professional licensure (PE, chartered status) is a plus but not required. Practical applied work outweighs credentials.

Reporting to the Vice President of Product, you will help establish reliable methods for measuring how often clients appear in AI answers, how they compare with competitors, and what factors influence those results.

This role combines data analytics, research, experimentation, and LLM evaluation. You will work with structured and unstructured data, develop measurement frameworks, evaluate AI search systems, and collaborate with product and engineering teams to define meaningful metrics. The focus is on producing reliable, transparent findings that help clients understand their performance and identify areas for improvement.

Track how frequently, favorably, and accurately clients appear in AI-generated answers compared with defined competitors, using rigorous baselines, sampling methods, and documented uncertainty.

Maintain evaluation rubrics, benchmarks, and processes for measuring agreement between raters.

Perform mouse handling and in-life procedures, including dosing by oral (PO), intraperitoneal (IP), subcutaneous (SC), and intravenous (IV) routes, tumor cell implantation, tumor and body-weight measurements, and in-life and terminal blood collection

Hands-on experience with oncology models (e.g., xenograft, syngeneic) and with murine models of inflammation or immunology

jobs.description:
What We Can Achieve Together

The Policy Research Associate will support the evaluation, prioritization and advancement of state and local policies that can provide effective and scalable contributions to the adoption of regenerative agriculture practices and water quality improvements across the country, primarily though not exclusively at the state level. They will work with interdisciplinary teams to identify, compile, and research promising water policy interventions, develop legislative or administrative solutions for those interventions, and work with government relations professionals and others to implement those solutions at the state or federal level. The Research Associate will help identify and foster relationships with third-party contractors, including consultants, other NGOs, universities, among others to build TNC’s policy research capabilities.

Responsibilities & Scope

May supervise administrative staff and/or volunteers, interns, or temporary staff.
Financial responsibility to complete projects appropriately and assist with budget development and meeting fundraising goals for local and worldwide conservation.
Ensures program compliance with internal policies and external requirements.
Works within scope of program’s strategic goals.
Provides research and policy analysis in support of legislative and/or policy priorities.
May aid with preparation of program materials including presentations, memos, and other communications.
Influences the outcome of policy and/or corporate initiatives at the federal, state, and local levels.
Develop strategic partnerships with relevant agencies, conservation organizations, and/or industry.
Work independently, working with supervisor as needed.
May require occasional domestic travel for multi-day retreats, meetings, and conferences
May work long/flexible hours as needed to coordinate with staff and partners across the US or region.

This is a full-time, 2-year grant-funded position with the possibility of extension based on continued grant funding. Working location is remote from a home office within the continental United States.

We’re Looking For You

The Policy Research Associate will play a vital role in the development and support of replicable policy interventions at the state and local level to advance the outcomes of the North America Agriculture Program’s Water Policy Accelerator. They will serve as a subject matter expert on projects with other teams and will be responsible for assisting our government relations staff in advancing interventions to water quality challenges. A priority area for this work will be to research and design policy interventions that expand the implementation of Edge of Field practices, such as vegetative buffers and wetlands, as well as identifying and developing policy solutions to other water policy challenges. This position will report into the North America Agriculture Program, working closely with an interdisciplinary team from North America Policy and Government Relations, Global Conservation Campaigns, numerous state Business Units, and external stakeholders. The Policy Research Associate will have strong analytical skills, experience in policy analysis, and an understanding of law and the legislative process. The successful candidate will be able to work effectively independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, highly matrixed organization; and be adaptable to shifting needs and priorities.

What You’ll Bring

Minimum Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree and 3 years related experience; or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Fluency in English
Experience researching information from divergent sources and compiling it into a cohesive reporting structure.
Experience with legislative or policy initiatives at the state level.
Experience presenting to and communicating with government or corporate staff and/or program leadership.
Experience working with partners and government agencies.

Desired Qualifications:
Juris Doctor Degree or Master’s Degree in Public Policy or related field.
Experience drafting legislation and negotiating with interested parties.
Experience developing or implementing federal or state policies, including funding/grant programs.
Experience with programs, laws and stakeholders who engage on agriculture, water and land-use policy related work in the United States.

Salary Information

The starting pay range for a candidate selected for this position is generally within the range of $60,000 - $85,000. This range only applies to candidates whose country of employment is the USA. Where a successful candidate’s actual pay will fall within this range will be based on a variety of factors, including, for example, the candidate's location, qualifications, specific skills, and experience. Please note countries outside the USA would have a different pay range in the local currency based on the local labor market, and not tied to USA pay or ranges. Your geographic location will be confirmed during the recruitment.

Who We Are

The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Whether it’s career development, flexible schedules, or a rewarding mission, there’s many reasons to love life inside TNC. Want a better insight to TNC? Check out our TNC Talent playlist on YouTube to hear stories from staff or visit Glassdoor.

One goal is to cultivate an inclusive work environment so that all our colleagues around the globe feel a sense of belonging and that their unique contributions to our mission are valued. In addition to the requirements in our job postings, we recognize that people come with talent and experiences outside of a job and consider each applicant’s unique experience. Please apply – we’d love to hear from you. To quote a popular saying at TNC, “you’ll join for the mission, and stay for the people.”

What We Bring

Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!

TNC offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package including health care benefits, flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) plan with an 8% employer match, parental leave, accrued paid time off, life insurance, disability coverage, employee assistance program, other life and work well-being benefits. Learn more about our Benefits and Perks here.

We’re proud to offer a flexible work environment that supports of the health and well-being of the people we employ.

Millions of people rely on digital maps every day to navigate, to discover, to find their way. But maps are only as accurate as the data behind them, and data is only as trustworthy as the people who verify it. Your knowledge of USA's geography, local landmarks, and how people actually navigate your region is something no algorithm can fully replicate. That local intelligence is what makes maps genuinely useful.

In this role, you will conduct structured quality audits on spatial and mapping datasets. Your role is to verify, evaluate, and validate complex geographic and business information using advanced mapping tools and detailed reference materials.

Be open to work across a diverse set of Task Types (e.g. Maps, News, Audio tasks, Relevance)
Provide structured feedback that helps refine mapping algorithms and improve geographic intelligence

Why this matters:
Accurately verified mapping data prevents real-world navigation errors. Your verification work ensures people can reliably find critical services, reach trusted businesses, and navigate with confidence. At scale, this is infrastructure work that is foundational to how billions of people interact with geographic information.

Extractions

Act as the auxiliary supervisor for all Multiuse Laboratories within the National University System.
Supervise the preparations for laboratory experiments and demonstrations for scheduled classes in close collaboration with university faculty.
Assist with and train multiuse laboratory staff on experiment set-ups. Assist instructors and students during laboratory classes.

Manage teams of technicians at the Spectrum, South Bay, Naval Hospital, Fresno, and Los Angeles locations.

Attention to detail.

In this role, you will own the data ecosystem spanning the entire clinician lifecycle—from the moment a provider enters our recruiting funnel, through onboarding, credentialing, and state licensing, to their ongoing clinical performance, operational efficiency, and downstream business impact on patient retention.

You will develop performance frameworks that merge operational SLAs (e.g., on-time arrival, inbox turnaround times) with clinical quality and safety metrics. Additionally, you will lead our efforts in provider interaction analytics, creating evaluation and scoring logic to quantify qualitative behavioral dimensions, such as clinician empathy from consultation transcripts. Sitting at the intersection of Clinical Operations, Quality, Talent, Business Strategy, and Product, you will serve as the primary analytical partner to our Clinical Leadership and Executive team.

What You’ll Do

Credentialing & Licensing Efficiency:
Build predictive frameworks and monitoring dashboards to reduce state-by-state licensing bottlenecks and decrease provider time-to-first-consultation.

Modern Analytics Stack & AI Tools:
Experience with cloud data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks) and active adoption of modern AI tools (e.g., LLMs for coding efficiency, automated insights) to accelerate analytics workflows.

Experience with cohort analysis, retention modeling, and constructing behavioral/qualitative scoring models.
